### G391 — The handoff's `extends`: deferred to 5-8, its construction built by 5-5 (M28)
- **Kind:** Choice (re-pin P8; plan `tier5-plans/repin/P8.md` §2.6; STATUS M28; parent plan §5) · **Specs:** PACKAGE
  MANAGER §12 l.1393-1405 (PKG-0338), l.1434-1435 (PKG-0347), l.1440-1441 (PKG-0351, TXT-0545), l.827; RUNTIME
  l.1300-1303; INTERFACE l.1717.
- **Description:** at 6cac8335 the handoff schema carries `? extends` (l.1401), the handoff preserves the declaration's
  `extends` (l.1434-1435), and the Runtime requires the descriptor's extended-contract set to match the handoff exactly
  (l.1441). No handoff exists before 5-5 and 5-8 (owner decision 1(a), 2026-11-13).
- **Decision:**
  - P8 does not build the handoff. PKG-0338, PKG-0347 and PKG-0351 stay deferred by name to work item 5-8, each with a
    `compared` record, and TXT-0545 rides PKG-0351 to 5-8.
  - **The Package Manager's side of the handoff, its construction (PM l.827), is built in 5-5 (TIER5-PLAN §5).** It must
    carry `extends` from the manifest's module declaration, without adding or widening (l.1434-1435); otherwise 5-8's
    exact match has nothing to compare.
  - P8 builds the Runtime's comparison of a supplied contract-reference set with the validated descriptor
    (`matchesContracts` with the extended set) for host-configuration and static records; 5-8 applies it to the handoff.
    A field the source omits is none or empty once it supplies any reference (G393, P8c), for the handoff too.
  - PKG-0351 and TXT-0545 leave `[deferred]` with a 5-8 test that carries both ids.
  - TXT-0545's baseline entry names no section; `spectrace` derives it from its lines (l.1401, l.1441: §12), so it rides
    PKG-0351 (re-pin P8b Q1).
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-19 by planning; recorded 2026-11-20 (re-pin P8b).

### G395 — The `lcn.storage_fetch` contract
- **Kind:** FREE (Tier 5 step 5-3a-1; plan `tier5-plans/step5-3a-trust.md` revision 5, §3.1; reviews and synthesis
  `tier5-plans/{opus,fable}-checks/step5-3a-*.md`) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER l.854-858 (the retrieval API of a
  Storage binding is implementation-defined and documented; PKG-0474), l.1453-1458 (no common fetch interface),
  l.397, l.443-444 (Storage content is untrusted); RUNTIME l.601-626 (application readiness in the module's own
  contract, no `NOT_READY` for it), l.3776-3783 (no path crosses a realization); INTERFACE l.141-192, l.345-346,
  l.446-458, l.1935; TRANSPORT l.371-378, l.826-843, l.1054-1058; CA l.244-247.
- **Description:** G91 (a) decided the contract and G136 its readiness signal; neither had a document. The owner
  ruled on 2026-11-20 that the Package Manager fetches packages only through the storage module, never by embedding
  libstorage or `logos-storage-nim`, and kept this contract over storage_module's own download methods (G91 (b)).
- **Decision:**
  - The interface `lcn.storage_fetch` (`sdk/src/logos_sdk/contracts/lcn_storage_fetch.cddl`, in `logos_sdk`, since
    storage_module sees only the SDK): `stat_object` (size), `read_object` (`object`, `offset: uint64`,
    `length: uint32`), `fetch_readiness` and `fetch_readiness_changed_event` (`starting`, `ready`, `offline`).
    Reads are stateless; no job, no session, no path, no transport choice.
  - `length` is 1 to 1,048,576 by rule, refused with `invalid-length` (a schema cannot bound it, INTERFACE
    l.446-458). A provider checks the length, then the locator, then availability (readiness and the object), then
    the range. A read answers exactly `min(length, size - offset)` bytes.
  - Failures are expected outcomes only, as response arms: `invalid-length`, `invalid-locator`, `not-ready`,
    `unavailable` (resume from the same offset: a locator's bytes are fixed), `out-of-range`. A provider not
    `ready` MAY serve an object it holds locally (plan Q4).
  - The root is computed from the document at regeneration (`lcn_storage_fetch_root.nim`), never typed by hand.
  - The reference fake `fetch_fake_module` (no configuration; objects derived from `fetch-fake/<size>/<seed>`;
    its own methods set readiness and faults) and the conformance harness `logos_sdk/testing/storagefetch` (call
    checks everywhere, readiness checks where handles subscribe) live in the SDK's testing package, for 5-3b and
    N-4.
  - The event needs the consumer's `subscribe-event` and the provider's `publish-event` (CA l.244-247; G140).
    Both ends of the Package Manager's route stay hosted (C1): payloads go between their processes directly.
  - `sdk/docs/STORAGE-FETCH.md` documents all of it; the locator encoding of storage_module (G5) comes with 5-3b
    and N-4, and PKG-0474 is claimed there.
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-20 by planning (plan rulings Q1-Q4, Q13, Q14); the owner kept the contract
  (2026-11-20); built 2026-11-20 (5-3a-1, I114).

### G396 — The package trust file v2
- **Kind:** FREE (Tier 5 step 5-3a-2; owner batch C, C2; plan `tier5-plans/step5-3a-trust.md` §3.2.1,
  §3.2.3) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER l.401-406 (continuity over profile selection, key mappings and
  exact-name authorization: PKG-0418 to PKG-0421), l.413-422 (exact names; TXT-0463, l.420), l.433-438,
  l.446-449 (a development anchor through the same path, PKG-0083), l.485-488, l.242 and l.498 (the
  bounds), l.531-537 (one 48-byte key per kid, PKG-0434; no shared kid, PKG-0107; no reuse, l.533); CA
  l.1309-1312; BCP l.403-406.
- **Description:** G137 and G299 put the package-signing anchors in logosd's revisioned trust file "in
  Tier 5", without its format. The Package Manager decodes the same input wherever it runs (C1 hosts it in
  its own process), so the document and its rules belong to core and continuity to the daemon.
- **Decision:** `<session>/trust.cbor` is `lcn.package_trust`, `logos-core-nim.trust.v2`
  (`src/logos_core/package/trustdoc.cddl`), closed: `revision`, `development` (D27's switch), `signing`
  (the baseline profile and every anchor: `kid`, `public_key`, `packages`, `development`), `catalog` and
  `provenance` (G398). One revision covers every field. The rules beyond the CDDL, in
  `package/trustdoc.nim`: the revision not below the floor; anchors in strictly ascending kid byte order
  (so kids are unique); each anchor's names non-empty and in strictly ascending UTF-8 byte order (so
  unique), so one content has one encoding and the mark's digest names contents; names compared byte for
  byte, none special; a key any 48 bytes, two kids may share one; the file's only bound 1 MiB, exported as
  `MaxTrustBytes` so the Package Manager applies the same (5-3b); a development anchor in force only while
  the switch is on (G137). Decoding and the rules are two steps: `decodeTrust` (schema only, so `trust
  show`, the offline `deployment` and `daemon config check` read a refused file) and `checkTrust`.
  `acceptedSigning` builds `package/trust.TrustInput` from the anchors in force through `addAnchor`, only
  for a file that passes every rule. logosd's start applies the rules at both reads and converts before
  continuity (G299 amended). `[IMPL]` A v1 file is still read as the v2 content with no anchor and
  nothing selected, with the digest of its own bytes (Q6); every writer writes v2.
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-20 (planning's rulings Q5, Q6, Q15 on the plan, both reviews agreeing);
  built in I114, part 5-3a-2a.

### G397 — `logosctl trust` for the package trust file, and key separation
- **Kind:** FREE (Tier 5 step 5-3a-2; plan `tier5-plans/step5-3a-trust.md` §3.2.3, §3.3) · **Specs:** PACKAGE
  MANAGER l.417 (each signer a non-empty set of exact names), l.420 (an added name is a later revision),
  l.436-437 (a removed anchor is withdrawn), l.531-534 (one 48-byte key per kid; the key used for nothing
  else, PKG-0435); CA l.1309-1312 (the call-evidence key used for nothing else).
- **Description:** G396 gives the trust file anchors; G303's `logosctl trust` writes only the switch, and
  nothing yet keeps a package-signing key apart from the session's call-evidence keys.
- **Decision:**
  - **Key separation** (built in 5-3a-2a): no anchor of the file, in force or not, uses a public key of the
    session's call evidence: every binding under `keys/`, retired ones included (a retired binding keeps its
    public key), and the binding beside the configured key when it lives elsewhere. logosd's start checks it
    after the rules and before continuity. `[IMPL]` A start reads the bindings for it only when the file
    names an anchor; a binding that cannot be read then refuses the start.
  - **The commands** (5-3a-2b), offline under the session lock: `trust show` with the profile, each anchor,
    whether it is in force, the selections and the reason a refused file is refused; `trust anchor add`,
    `remove`, `add-names` and `remove-names`; `trust development on|off`; `trust reestablish --revision N`,
    which applies the rules and key separation before it writes a mark. Every writer validates its result
    with the rules logosd applies, writes revision + 1, and writes nothing for a change that changes
    nothing. No command selects a catalog or provenance profile (G398).
  - **As built** (5-3a-2b; the absent withdrawals and the JSON in 5-3a-2c): every writer edits the current file once (`withAnchor`, `withoutAnchor`,
    `withNames`, `withoutNames`, `withDevelopment` in `daemon/trustfile.nim`) and ends in `commitTrust`,
    which checks the result with `validateTrust`: the schema and the 1 MiB bound, `checkTrust`, key
    separation and `acceptedSigning`, what a start applies before continuity. The evidence keys are read
    when the file before or after names an anchor, as at a start. `[IMPL]` `KID` is text or `hex:` and hex
    digits (I41's spelling); `HEX` is 96 hex digits or `@FILE` holding them alone or as `lcn-pkg keygen`'s
    `public key:` line, surrounding whitespace ignored. `[IMPL]` Names are taken as given, 1 to 128 bytes,
    and the command puts them in canonical order, each once. `[IMPL]` Q16's rule (ruled after Fable,
    planning 2026-11-21; PM l.119 leaves it to the implementation): a command that adds or sets what is
    already so is unchanged (exit 0, "unchanged", `"changed": false`): names already present, the same
    anchor again, the switch as it is. One that withdraws what is not there is refused (exit 1, nothing
    written): `anchor remove` of a kid that names no anchor ("no anchor has kid HEX"), and `remove-names`,
    all or nothing, with any name the anchor does not authorize byte for byte (PM l.418-419), each such
    name named. A mistyped withdrawal then fails instead of leaving the key or name it meant in force, and
    "the kid names an anchor" is one rule for `remove`, `add-names` and `remove-names`. A kid already
    present with another key, marker or names is refused. `[IMPL]` Q17's
    line ends every refusal the current file already earns, not only a selection, and a writer whose change
    changes nothing refuses such a file too; a change that removes the cause is written. `trust
    development` reports how many development anchors enter or leave force. `trust reestablish` refuses a
    file `validateTrust` refuses, and writes no mark. `trust show` decodes without the rules and shows the
    anchors, the selections and `refusal`, the reason a start would give, with continuity "not reached"
    for a file the rules refuse (JSON per G89, `docs/DAEMON.md` §6). `[IMPL]` In its JSON, `kid_text` is
    given only when `--kid` would read the text back as the same kid, so not for a text beginning `hex:`;
    `in_force` is what the file says (switch and marker), not what a running logosd uses; and `trust
    development`'s `development_anchors` counts the anchors the file marks `development`, changed or not.
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-20 (planning's rulings Q16, Q17 on the plan); key separation built in I114,
  part 5-3a-2a; the commands built in part 5-3a-2b (`daemon/trustfile.nim`, `daemon/render.nim`,
  `src/logosctl.nim`; `test_daemon_config` suite `dc.trustctl`, `test_logosd`); the refused withdrawals
  and the JSON names in part 5-3a-2c, on planning's ruling after Fable's answers (2026-11-21).

### G398 — Catalog and provenance selections in the package trust file
- **Kind:** FREE (C3, C9; Tier 5 step 5-3a-2; plan `tier5-plans/step5-3a-trust.md` §3.2.1) · **Specs:**
  PACKAGE MANAGER l.401 ("profile selection" under the revision), l.453-459 (a selected catalog profile's
  anchoring only through protected input), l.733-738 (only protected policy selects a provenance profile;
  its continuity covers the absence of a selection; one counter allowed), l.740-745 (none selected: the
  baseline; an unsupported selection rejected before package material is accepted, PKG-0169), l.862 (a
  source's provenance locator selects nothing); BCP l.409-410.
- **Description:** PKG-0418's "profile selection" and PM l.736's "the absence of a selected profile" need a
  field under the revision, and C9's "a configuration that asks for a profile is refused" needs something
  a file can ask. cdCDDLe has neither `null` nor `[+ …]`.
- **Decision:** the package trust file has two required sections, `catalog` and `provenance`, each
  `lcn.trust_selection = { ? selected: tstr .size (1..128) }`; an empty section selects none, so the file
  always states each selection. No catalog profile is built in Tier 5 (C9) and no provenance profile until
  step 5-11 (C3): a file with `selected` in either decodes, then `checkTrust` refuses it naming the
  profile, before continuity, so a refused revision never moves the mark. The refusal is in
  `package/trustdoc.nim`, so the Package Manager refuses the same file (5-3b). Nothing else selects: a
  manifest field is refused by its decoder, and a source's `provenance_object` is location data
  (PKG-0166). 5-11 adds the provenance section's signers, builders, bindings and limits, with a new format
  identifier if it adds a required field; until then an unknown field is refused, so older code fails
  closed.
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-20 (planning's rulings Q7, Q8, Q19); built in I114, part 5-3a-2a.

### G399 — The Package Manager's protected input
- **Kind:** FREE (Tier 5 step 5-3b; plan `tier5-plans/step5-3b-plan.md` §3.1) · **Specs:** CONFIGURATION l.58
  (configuration never carries protected trust input); PACKAGE MANAGER l.401-406 (trust continuity), l.740-745 (an
  unsupported selection rejected before package material is accepted, PKG-0169), l.854-858 (deployment-configured
  Storage bindings); DEPLOYMENT §2 (protected input changes offline, at the next start).
- **Description:** the Package Manager needs its trust input, its Storage bindings and its protected catalog. None
  may be module configuration, and since C1 hosts it in its own process it must check whatever it receives itself.
- **Decision:**
  - **The value** (5-3b-1): one deterministic-CBOR value, closed, `lcn.pm_input`
    (`src/logos_core/pm/input.cddl`), `logos-core-nim.pm-input.v1`: `trust` (the package trust file's accepted
    bytes, 1 byte to 1 MiB), `storage` (the bindings, `{binding, instance}`), `catalog` (`{storage, object,
    digest}`, G401) and optional `limits` (`archive_bytes` up to 1 GiB, default 1 GiB; `catalog_bytes` up to
    4 MiB, default 4 MiB; `catalog_entries` up to 65,536, default 65,536; `cache_entries` up to 4,096, default 256;
    `read_deadline_ms` up to 86,400,000, default 300,000, G402). Our CDDL has no `+`, so `storage` is `[* …]` and
    an empty list is refused by rule, as G396's anchor names are.
  - **The check** (`pm/input.nim`, `decodePmInput`): at most 16 MiB, deterministic CBOR, the closed map, the format, at least one
    binding, binding names unique, `catalog.storage` one of them, each bound within its range (a bound of 0 is
    refused), then `trustdoc`'s decoding and rules on `trust`, so a catalog or provenance selection is refused
    here as at logosd's start (G398, G404). The first failure refuses the whole value, naming the field and never
    quoting the bytes.
  - `[IMPL]` The value is fixed for one start (Q10): a trust change, a new catalog or a new binding applies at the
    next start.
  - **The resolver limits** (planning's ruling of 2026-11-22, with Fable's review, `fable-checks/step5-3b-plan.md`
    §6; PM l.1241-1254): `resolver_limits`, all four limits, is a required field of `lcn.pm_input`, decoded by
    `decodeResolverLimits` and carried in `PmInput` (`initEngine` has no separate parameter, so no caller can pass
    values the input does not hold). The Package Manager has no default: an absent or out-of-range limit fails its
    initialization, naming the field, before any root operation (l.1251, l.1253). The format name stays
    `pm-input.v1`: no released logosd wrote one.
  - **The daemon's section** (5-3b-2; DAEMON.md §3): `package_manager` `{instance, storage, catalog,
    ? resolver_limits, ? limits}` in `daemon_config.cddl`, the `lcn.pm_*` rules resolved with `pm/input.cddl` as
    one document. Check 2's part (`daemon/config.nim`, `checkPackageManager`, right after the names check): the
    instance and every binding's instance are `hosted_dynamic` operator entries of `modules` (C1 of the plan: no
    archive in logosd's process); the Package Manager's has a `state_assignment` and no configuration; at least
    one binding, each name once, none naming the Package Manager; `catalog.storage` one of them; then the composed
    value passes `decodePmInput`. Compose (`protectedInputsOf`) puts the bytes in `protected_inputs` for that
    instance only; the trust bytes are the v2 encoding of the trust state the start accepted.
  - **logosd's preset** (the ruling's C1 to C4): `daemon/config.nim`'s four constants, the same on every platform
    and build mode, never computed from the machine (PM l.1279-1280). C1: the section's `resolver_limits` holds all
    four keys or is absent, so a partial set fails check 1 and no key is filled from the preset. C2: the preset
    applies only when the section names none. C3: a change of the preset changes results for an unchanged
    configuration (PM l.1314-1315), so it is a new row here and a release note, and DEPLOYMENT §12 tells an
    operator who needs fixed results to write the four values; each start logs the values it composed and their
    origin (`package_manager: <instance> gets resolver limits … (logosd's preset)`), for the operator's log only
    (l.1514). C4: logosd checks the values at start through the Package Manager's decoder, and the instance checks
    them again. DAEMON.md's `package_manager` row states the values under `test_daemon_config`'s word-for-word
    test. The values are G443's.
  - **A tripped limit is the operator's to see** (the ruling's M5 and S1): exhaustion answers
    `dependency-unavailable`, as a missing dependency does (l.1501-1502), so the resolver records which limit ended
    the operation (`ResolverCounters.limit`) and the engine logs it with its value ("a root operation stopped at
    the resolver limit … (N)"). The two depth refusals no longer carry the depth reached, which would show the limit
    to the caller (`pmtest_module`'s `resolve` returns the message, as the §15 methods will).
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-21 (planning's rulings on the plan, Q3 and Q4) and 2026-11-22 (the resolver limits);
  the value and its check built in part 5-3b-1 (I116); the resolver limits, the daemon's section, its checks,
  compose and the preset in part 5-3b-2.

### G400 — The protected realization input
- **Kind:** FREE (Tier 5 step 5-3b; plan `tier5-plans/step5-3b-plan.md` §3.2) · **Specs:** LOADER l.16, l.474 (the
  private Runtime-to-Loader handoff is implementation-defined), l.282 (the state directory), l.368-370 (idempotency
  over the private handoff); RUNTIME l.1600-1601 (protected construction input); CONFIGURATION l.21, l.58.
- **Description:** G399's value must reach the hosted Package Manager at initialization without being module
  configuration and without a carrier change (Q10).
- **Decision (planning's ruling Q4, design (A), with Fable's review F1):** the host configuration's
  `protected_inputs` (`{instance, input}`, not for secrets) is kept by the Runtime for the instance's life and
  handed to the Loader in the attempt's side-table entry; the Loader writes it to
  `<state_dir>/.lcn-protected-input` around initialization, relative to a directory descriptor, through a random
  temporary name, following no link, and removes it after initialization, at release and at retirement. A
  directory at the reserved name fails the realization; an attempt without input removes a leftover. State
  transfer skips the name. No isolation between processes of one user is claimed (D16): any process of logosd's
  user can replace the file between the write and the read.
- **As built** (5-3b-2): `lcn.app_protected_input` in `host_config.cddl` (1 byte to 16 MiB; the instance listed,
  with a state assignment, once; "protected_inputs: <instance> …" at `create`, naming the instance, never the
  bytes). The engine copies each into the side table once (`sidetable`, before any thread starts) and each
  attempt's inbound entry points at its instance's copy. `runtime/protinput.nim` writes, reads and removes the
  file: `openat` on the state directory, `fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)` on the reserved name, `unlinkat` of
  anything but a directory, the bytes to `.lcn-protected-input.<32 hex>` created `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`
  mode 0600 (four names tried), `fsync`, `renameat`, then the directory flushed; on Windows, for direct
  realizations only, `CREATE_NEW` with `FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT` and `MoveFileExW`. The Loader writes it once
  the attempt's state directory is established, before `_MODULE_init` or before the Module Host starts, removes it
  when initialization returns and again at release; the Runtime removes it at retirement; a `copy` transfer skips
  the name and its temporary names. The bytes' BLAKE3-256 is part of the realization request's key (L l.368-370).
  The Package Manager's shell reads it once in `_MODULE_init` (`readProtectedInput`, bounded at 16 MiB) and logs a
  refusal, since the Runtime records only `_MODULE_init`'s code.
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-21 (planning's ruling Q4 on the plan); built in part 5-3b-2 (I116).

### G401 — The catalog document, the protected catalog and its acquisition
- **Kind:** FREE (amends G90, replaces G150; Tier 5 step 5-3b; plan §3.3) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER l.834-835
  (catalog formats, acquisition, refresh and catalog-policy configuration are implementation-defined, documented,
  and keep §4.1 to §4.4; PKG-0472, PKG-0473), l.866-868 and §6 (an entry is `{identity, source}`, location only;
  PKG-0115), l.467-469 and l.591 (a signature or catalog proves no freshness; PKG-0112), l.478-480 (lost state;
  optional catalog data invalidates nothing installed), l.886-887 (an unimplemented source profile), l.1308-1309
  (unavailable material), l.1328-1331 (protected catalog policy; the protected catalog lists retained sources),
  l.1657 (the order of `list_packages`); STORAGE-FETCH §3 (a locator names fixed bytes).
- **Description:** G90 (a) chose an unsigned `{format, sequence, entries}` document with its locator in the daemon
  configuration and a lower sequence refused; G150 had `catalog set` and `catalog refresh` restart the Package
  Manager instance. PM l.1328 and l.1331 name a protected catalog and protected catalog policy without defining
  them, and l.834 leaves both to us.
- **Decision:**
  - **The document** `lcn.package_catalog` (`src/logos_core/pm/catalog.cddl`), deterministic CBOR, closed:
    `format` `logos-core-nim.catalog.v1`, `sequence` (uint64), `entries` (PM §6's `package_catalog_entry`).
    Entries in canonical order (package-name bytes ascending, SemVer precedence descending, the source record's
    deterministic-CBOR bytes ascending), each `{identity, source}` once; one identity may have several sources.
    `[IMPL]` At most `catalog_bytes` and `catalog_entries`, the size `stat_object` states checked before any read.
    Any refusal refuses the whole document and changes nothing. A `nix` entry is kept and never used
    (`unsupported-source`).
  - **The protected catalog** is the document protected input names by binding, locator and BLAKE3-256 digest
    (G399); bytes with another digest are refused before they are decoded, so a provider cannot substitute an
    older still-signed document (PM l.467-469). **Protected catalog policy:** none; two acceptable manifests for one
    identity with different commitments fail `dependency-unavailable`, as the resolver does.
  - **No refresh.** A locator names fixed bytes and the digest pins them, so reading it again cannot give a newer
    document. A new catalog is a new locator and digest, set offline, applying at logosd's next start (DEPLOYMENT
    §2). This replaces G150: no `catalog set` or `catalog refresh` restarts the Package Manager (restarting a bound
    system service is the open TF-45). The documented cost: a new package version needs a new catalog, and a new
    catalog restarts every module of the node.
  - `[IMPL]` **Acquisition:** the configured document is read once its binding's provider reports `ready`; a read
    that fails is retried on the next `ready` and after a back-off (1 s doubling to 60 s) while it stays `ready`. One
    accepted or refused document ends acquisition for the start. The Package Manager never waits on Storage at
    start; with no catalog in use an operation that needs one fails `package-unavailable`, never as if empty.
  - **The kept catalog** (amends G90): the last accepted document, with its binding, locator and digest, is kept in
    the Package Manager's state directory (`catalog.kept`, `lcn.pm_catalog_kept`), written by sync and rename; the
    catalog is in use whether or not the write succeeds. At start it is in use only while its locator and digest
    equal the configured ones; a kept catalog never stands in for another configured one. A kept file that does
    not decode is set aside and logged.
  - **Sequence continuity** (G90 (a)): a document read is accepted when its sequence is greater than the kept
    one's, or equal with equal bytes; a lower one, or an equal one with other bytes, is refused and logged. The
    sequence orders documents and claims no freshness (C9; PKG-0112); it is not under the trust file's revision.
    After the state directory is lost the first document read is accepted. A deliberate rollback is a new document
    under a higher sequence.
  - **`lcn-pkg catalog SOURCE.edn --sequence:N`** writes the canonical document of the entries given and prints its
    digest; it refuses a repeated entry and anything the Package Manager would refuse, and signs nothing.
  - `docs/PACKAGE-MANAGER.md` §3 documents all of it (PKG-0472).
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-21 (planning's rulings on the plan, with Fable's review F2; G150 was an implementation
  default, never an owner question); built in part 5-3b-1 (I116).

### G402 — Storage bindings, routes and retrieval
- **Kind:** FREE (Tier 5 step 5-3b; plan §3.4) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER l.854-858 (a binding, its retrieval
  API documented; PKG-0474), l.397, l.443-444 (Storage content is untrusted), l.1308-1309, §13 (PKG-0353);
  STORAGE-FETCH §3, §4 (fixed bytes, resume from an offset, readiness); RUNTIME l.3072-3082 (a replayed
  establishment revives nothing), l.3081, l.3089-3096 (renewal); TRANSPORT l.826-828 (the caller's deadline);
  BCP l.557-558 (foreign text).
- **Description:** G91 (a) and G395 give the contract; nothing yet says how the Package Manager holds its routes,
  retries, or bounds one call.
- **Decision:**
  - **A binding** is a name and an `lcn.storage_fetch` provider instance (G399). An LGX source's `storage` names
    one; a source naming no configured binding has material that cannot be located (`package-unavailable`), and
    the name is logged once per start.
  - **Routes:** one per binding, then `fetch_readiness_changed_event` and `fetch_readiness`. Every establishment has
    a new `request_key` (128 random bits); a key is reused only to retry an establishment whose response was lost,
    `[IMPL]` at most three times. A lost route (its route end, or a call finding it unusable) is renewed under a new
    key; a renewal refused as unknown, closed, failed or revoked releases it and establishes a new one. `[IMPL]` A
    refused establishment is retried after a back-off, 1 s doubling to 60 s. Upkeep stops when `_MODULE_destroy`
    begins (G437). Route generations count every time a route becomes ready, so a stale loss report for a renewed
    route is ignored.
  - **Retrieval**, `[IMPL]` one object at a time per binding: `stat_object`, the size bound checked before any read,
    `unavailable` there not retried (planning, 2026-11-21); `read_object` in 1 MiB steps with BLAKE3-256 computed
    while reading; a mid-object `unavailable` retried from its offset after 1, 2 and 4 s, at most three times in a
    row; `not-ready` or a lost route waits for `ready` or a new route, bounded by the deadline, then the same call
    again; anything else (`invalid-locator`, `out-of-range`, `invalid-length`, an invocation error, a call past its
    deadline, a short or long answer) ends the retrieval as unavailable, the provider's `detail` logged as foreign
    text. The bytes stay untrusted until the pinned digest (the catalog) or `openLgx` (an archive) verifies them.
  - `[IMPL]` **The deadline** `read_deadline_ms`, 300 s by default, bounds one call and the wait for `ready` after
    `not-ready`: above storage_module's longest call at its defaults (120 s direct, 180 s private) and its 120 s
    network phase. It catches a provider that broke its own bound; availability comes from `unavailable`. The
    engine also runs its own timer per call, so a provider that never answers still ends the call, and a late
    answer is ignored.
  - **`provenance_object` is never read** (PKG-0167, until 5-11).
  - **The bindings in logosd** (5-3b-2): `package_manager.storage` (G399). The locator encodings are
    STORAGE-FETCH §5's table, which gains the fake's `fetch-fake/state/<name>` (1 to 64 bytes of
    `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -`, no leading `.`; the file `<state_dir>/objects/<name>`, read at each call; §12 Q1 (c) of
    the plan), so a hosted test serves an exact catalog and signed archives (PKG-0474 with PACKAGE-MANAGER.md §4).
  - **The provider of a route** `[IMPL]` (5-3b-2): a route names a provider record, whose id the Runtime assigns
    (`p-…`), not an instance. Before each establishment the shell looks up the binding's instance with
    `list_modules {instance}` and takes that record's `provider`; a lookup that gets no response counts as a lost
    establishment, any other failure as a refusal.
  - **The derived grants** (5-3b-2; DAEMON.md §5; amends G140): under `capability-authority`, with a
    `package_manager` section, logosd adds S9 to S11. S9: the Package Manager may call `establish_route`,
    `renew_route`, `close_route` and `list_modules`, in one rule with no `targets`; a deny of every Runtime
    Control event (as S3); and provider access to `lcn.storage_fetch` at the providers for `call`,
    `establish-route` and `renew-route` over the three methods' roots. S10: `subscribe-event` for `fetch_readiness_changed`. S11: the providers may publish it. The providers
    are the bindings' instances, each once, in byte order, as every policy set is.
  - **S9's Runtime Control rule names no `targets`** (planning's ruling of 2026-11-22 with Fable's review,
    `fable-checks/step5-3b-plan.md` §7.3). A first build gave `list_modules` its own rule with `targets` the
    providers, and the hosted test's lookup was refused: a list is decided once with no subject (I86), and a rule
    with `targets` never contains a request without selectors (`authority/policy.nim`). The spec's model for
    partial visibility is a narrowed allow (CA l.124, l.299-301, l.556; RUNTIME l.1543, l.3231, l.3235), which the
    Runtime applies record by record; CA l.124 permits narrowing and does not require it, and this authority never
    narrows (AUTHORITY-POLICY.md). So the rule conforms, and so would no targeted form of it: `establish_route` is
    decided with no target either, and `renew_route` and `close_route` name a route, which a rule with `targets`
    never contains. S6 gives `lcn_call` an untargeted `list_modules` the same way. **What is wider:** the Package
    Manager can read every module record of the Runtime (module names, instances, provider addresses, states,
    contracts, failure classes with their reasons); it uses one lookup by `instance` per binding
    (`pm/shell.nim`), and listing grants no authority to call a listed provider (RUNTIME l.3217).
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-21 (planning's rulings on the plan, with Fable's review F3 on request keys); retrieval,
  routes and their tests built in part 5-3b-1 (I116) over scripted providers; the hosted case, the provider
  lookup, the grants and the locator documentation in part 5-3b-2.

### G403 — The verification cache and trust in use
- **Kind:** FREE (C5; Tier 5 step 5-3b; plan §3.5) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER l.403-405 (retained provenance never
  substitutes for current trust), l.429-438 and l.435 (rotation MAY overlap, PKG-0079; a removed or revoked anchor
  is not used, PKG-0080), the cache MAY of PKG-0076 and its re-judgement PKG-0077, PKG-0081 and PKG-0082 (no
  catalog or Storage content adds trust), PKG-0114 (a detached signature verifies nothing).
- **Description:** C5 asks that rotation, removal and caching follow the text; the Package Manager needs a rule for
  what a cached verification may answer.
- **Decision:**
  - `[IMPL]` One entry per verified archive, keyed by the BLAKE3-256 of its bytes: the signer (profile, kid, key),
    the identity, the manifest commitment, the selected variant and the resolver's inspection. In memory, at most
    `cache_entries`, least recently used first out. Only an archive that verified is cached; archive bytes are not
    (installation keeps them, 5-5). The platform, limits and path rules are fixed for the start and not in the key.
  - **Every hit is judged again** against the trust input in use: the entry stands only while an anchor with the
    same kid holds the same key, under the same profile, authorizing the exact package name; otherwise it is
    dropped and the archive opened again, which then fails `signature-verification-failed`. Removal, revocation, a
    withdrawn name, a withdrawn development anchor and a new key for one kid each drop the entries they affect, and
    only those. The trust input is fixed within a start (Q10), so the tests drive the cache with two inputs; the
    rule is written so that 5-5, which persists installed state, keeps it.
  - **Rotation:** two anchors authorizing one name are both in force while the trust file lists both; the operator
    ends the overlap by removing the old one. PKG-0080 is claimed by 5-5; 5-3b carries its inspection half. The
    answer to PM l.408 stays no (G166).
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-21 (planning's rulings on the plan); built in part 5-3b-1 (I116,
  `src/logos_core/pm/vcache.nim`).

### G404 — Freshness: the baseline only
- **Kind:** FREE (C9; Tier 5 step 5-3b; plan §3.6) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER §4.2 (PKG-0085 to PKG-0093,
  PKG-0449), l.467-469, l.591 (PKG-0112), l.740-745; BCP l.409-410.
- **Description:** C9 builds no catalog profile in Tier 5; each §4.2 unit needs a stated disposition.
- **Decision:** no §4.2 profile exists. A trust file that selects one is refused by `trustdoc.checkTrust` (G398), at
  logosd's start and again by the Package Manager's input check (G399), so it never starts with one. The catalog
  document is closed and has no profile, key, log, checkpoint or minimum-version field. PKG-0085 and PKG-0449: the
  deployment claims the baseline and documents that it provides no authenticated catalog ordering, freshness or
  external anchoring (`docs/PACKAGE-MANAGER.md` §6). PKG-0086, PKG-0087, PKG-0090: no profile to identify, a selection
  refused. PKG-0088: entries carry no evidence. PKG-0089, PKG-0091, PKG-0092: nothing can require revocation lists,
  minimum versions or fresh evidence, so none is enforced, kept or re-established; signer state is the trust file's
  revision, continuity and not freshness. PKG-0093: a failed catalog read keeps the catalog in use and invalidates
  nothing. PKG-0112: no field, result, log line or document calls the sequence or a signature fresh.
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-21 (planning's rulings on the plan); built in part 5-3b-1 (I116).

### G405 — Resolution over asynchronous retrieval: the driver and the engine
- **Kind:** IMPL (Tier 5 step 5-3b; plan §3.7) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER l.1294-1295 (eligibility when reached, in
  order), l.1308-1310 (unavailable material; no lower candidate after a solution), §11 (the resolver, claimed).
- **Description:** the resolver calls its `Inspector` synchronously; retrieval is a sequence of calls on a route.
- **Decision:**
  - **The driver** (`pm/driver.nim`) runs the resolver over a memo of inspections keyed by the source record's
    deterministic-CBOR bytes. The first miss of a run is recorded and answered `ikUnavailable`; the driver then
    discards that run, retrieves the source, inspects it through the cache (G403), memoizes the inspection and runs
    again. The resolver is deterministic, so each run reaches the same candidate with its material: the candidates
    retrieved are exactly those a synchronous run reaches, in its order. A failed retrieval memoizes `ikUnavailable`
    (`package-unavailable`, never ineligible). A `nix` source is ineligible (`unsupported-source`) without a
    retrieval. The runs are bounded by the resolver's limits; archive bytes are dropped after inspection.
  - **The engine** (`pm/engine.nim`) owns the input, the catalog state, the bindings and their routes, the
    retrievals, the cache and the driver. It does no I/O: its entry points return commands (route operations, calls
    with their deadlines, timers, the kept-catalog write, replies, log lines) and it takes results back as events,
    so 5-3b-1 tests it in one process over scripted providers. `resolve` answers one root; with no catalog in use it
    is `package-unavailable`. `[IMPL]` The resolver's limits are a parameter of the engine: the shell or 5-4 chooses
    their source.
  - **The shell** (5-3b-2, `pm/shell.nim`) carries the engine's commands out on the instance's module thread under
    the confined kit (G335 to G338): `openShell` at `_MODULE_init` reads and checks the protected input (G400),
    loads `catalog.kept` bounded by `catalog_bytes` plus 8 KiB, makes a `RouteSet` and the engine, and starts it
    once `_MODULE_init` returned (`callSoon`). Route callbacks only queue events, and one task drains the queue, so
    no engine step runs inside a kit callback and none re-enters another. Calls are `invokeAsync` futures; a
    replaced route is released once its calls end, never from its own callbacks. Timers are chronos futures. The
    kept catalog is written with `writeAtomic`. `resolveRoot` returns a future that owns its cancellation (the
    engine answers it). `closeShell`, from an async `destroyModule`, stops the engine, cancels timers and calls,
    waits up to 10 s for its tasks, answers pending operations `package-unavailable` and closes the route set.
    The engine and the driver are `{.gcsafe.}`. `chronos` joins `layers.toml`'s `pm_external_allowlist` for the
    shell (G406's closure rule still refuses any storage library).
  - **The test module** `pmtest_module` (`tests/kit/pmtest_module.cddl`, `tests/kit/pmtest_impl.nim`) wraps the
    shell with `status` (catalog, bindings, pending) and `resolve` (an exact root; the closure with each package's
    schema root, or the error code and at most 512 bytes of the message, cut at a UTF-8 boundary), its primary
    contract, until 5-6a gives the Package Manager its name and its §15 methods.
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-21 (planning's ruling Q7 on the plan); the driver and the engine built in part 5-3b-1
  (I116); the shell and `pmtest_module` in part 5-3b-2.

### G406 — No storage library in the Package Manager
- **Kind:** FREE (owner, 2026-11-20; Tier 5 step 5-3b; plan §3.8) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER l.1453-1458 (no common
  fetch interface; the binding's API is ours).
- **Description:** the owner ruled that the Package Manager fetches only through storage_module, never by embedding
  libstorage or `logos-storage-nim` (G395). Nothing yet keeps a storage library out.
- **Decision:**
  - **The lint** `tools/lint/nostorage.py` (the flake check `lint-nostorage`) reads every nimble file's `requires`
    and switches, `config.nims`' switches, `nimble.lock`'s names and URLs, `nix/nimble-deps.json`, `flake.nix`'s
    inputs (comments aside) and every node of `flake.lock`, and the link and build pragmas (`passL`, `passC`,
    `link`, `compile`, `dynlib`, `header`) of `src/logos_core/pm/`, `src/logos_core/package/` and their
    in-repository import closure. None may name an entry of `tools/lint/nostorage.toml`'s deny list (`libstorage`,
    `logos-storage`, `logos_storage`, `storage-nim`, `codex`, `nim-codex`, `libcodex`, without case), which is
    reviewed like `layers.toml`. `--self-test` plants one violation of each kind in a clean tree (fixtures in the
    script) and checks that each fails.
  - **The layer rule** (`layers.toml`'s `pm_roots` and `pm_external_allowlist`, `layers.py`'s `pm-external`): the
    Package Manager's import closure may reach only the listed external packages (`results`, `zlib`), so a storage
    library under a name the deny list does not know fails too; an allowlist entry nothing reaches is itself an
    error.
  - **Scope:** the whole repository today; core's and the daemon's repositories after the split. The node's
    end-to-end flake (N-6) takes storage_module as an input on purpose and is outside it. N-4's bundle arrives
    through `LCN_STORAGE_FETCH_PROVIDER` at test time and is in no dependency list.
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-21 (planning's ruling Q8 on the plan, with Fable's review F5 keeping the flake-input
  check); built in part 5-3b-1 (I116).

### G443 — logosd's preset of the resolver limits
- **Kind:** IMPL (Tier 5 step 5-3b-2; planning's ruling of 2026-11-22, M4, with Fable's review
  `fable-checks/step5-3b-plan.md` §7.1 and §7.2) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER l.1241-1254 (the four limits, from
  protected policy; the maxima documented), l.1263 (an ineligible record is charged as a candidate), l.1279-1280
  (exhaustion and counters never depend on an implementation-local threshold), l.1314-1315 (a changed limit may
  change results).
- **Description:** under G399's C1 to C4 logosd's preset is the limits a deployment gets by writing none, and only
  the limits can end a run: no time budget may (l.1279-1280). 5-3b-2's measurement (CONFORMANCE "Resolver
  limits") found one step of the wide shape at about 14.5 h at the maxima, and honest closures too past the 1 s
  target at large sizes.
- **Options:** (a) the maxima (G361), with their cost stated; (b) moderate values, chosen by what honest closures
  need; (c) values chosen to meet the 1 s target with today's code (names about 2,048, attempts about 20).
- **Decision:** (b).
  - **The values** (`daemon/config.nim`'s four constants; DAEMON.md §3's `package_manager` row):

    | Limit | Preset | Why |
    |---|---|---|
    | `partial_closure_names` | 256 | real closures are tens of names; this is about ten times that |
    | `dependency_depth` | 32 | honest depth is a few edges |
    | `candidates_per_name` | 256 | room for a run of newer releases that are ineligible here, each charged (l.1263); Fable offered 64, planning took 256 |
    | `assignment_attempts` | 1,024 | one attempt per name, four times over for backtracking |

  - **Chosen by need, not by today's cost**, so the cost fix below does not change them; a change of the preset is a
    change of results (C3), so they are set before any deployment exists.
  - **Relations** (`test_daemon_config`, on the constants): attempts at least names, or a full closure cannot be
    bound; depth below names; each within its maximum.
  - **Not (c):** 20 attempts is below honest need (ruling M5). **Not (a):** at the maxima the limits protect no
    deployment that did not choose them, and any accepted signer with a package in the closure can reach the worst
    case, not only the root's.
  - **The maxima stay** (G361): they are the stated support (l.1252), and an operator who writes them has chosen
    them. DEPLOYMENT §12 says what raising a limit costs.
  - **What the preset costs today** is CONFORMANCE "Resolver limits"' table, measured on the Mac and on Linux. The
    wide shape with one 80,000-entry manifest still misses the 1 s target at the preset (about 50 ms per attempt,
    so about 51 s for its longest step at 1,024 attempts), and CONFORMANCE says so; `assignment_attempts` is the
    lever.
  - **CI asserts counts, not time** (ruling M6): the bench's shapes are `tests/support/pmshapes.nim`, which
    `tools/pmbench.nim` times and `test_pm_driver`'s suite "the resolver measurement's shapes, by their counts"
    asserts at small sizes, at the preset where it applies; the counters are deterministic.
  - **The cost fix is a step of its own after 5-3b** (planning's ruling, 7.2): incremental depths with a trail
    restored in reverse, the unresolved names kept ordered, a run that resumes instead of rerunning from the root
    (G405's driver), and slicing by a fixed count of work, so no result or counter changes. Its oracle is the
    present resolver on generated catalogs, compared on outcome and every counter. **Gate:** before 5-5, or before
    the first step that lets a consumer other than the operator's tools start a root operation, whichever comes
    first. Until then the figures stated for the preset are the size of the harm.
  - **The one resolver change in 5-3b-2** is `bindCand`'s single cycle walk (G361's amendment).
  - **Two editorial remarks** are in the spec owner's comments document, filed by Fable, and stop nothing:
    logos-lips `17284d73` (no limit counts dependency entries, and l.1280 keeps an implementation from bounding
    them itself) and `f19745f8` (the spec does not define a partial closure; we count bound names only).
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-22 (planning's ruling M4); built in part 5-3b-2 (I116). Planning reports the values to
  the owner.

### G444 — The installation root, its layout and its scope
- **Kind:** IMPL (Tier 5 step 5-5; plan `tier5-plans/step5-5-plan.md` §4.1; the scope is the owner's answer to Q5,
  (a), of 2026-11-22) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER l.924 (paths compared under the installation filesystem's rules),
  l.926-933 (the root; its layout and scope are deployment choices; no implicit sharing; a shared mutable root needs
  ownership, serialization and recovery, or is rejected; the rules documented), l.963 (every regular file of the
  selected variant), l.1180-1185 (`local_path`; resource access; a native library is a declared artifact).
- **Description:** the spec leaves the root's place, layout, scope and path rules to the deployment, and asks that
  they be documented.
- **Decision:**
  - **Where:** `<state_dir>/install/`, inside the instance's own assigned state directory, beside
    `.lcn-protected-input` and `catalog.kept`. `pm/store.openStore` takes the state directory as a parameter; 5-5-4
    places it in the shell's start.
  - **Layout:**
    - `install/lock`, `durable.nim`'s lock, held for the store's life;
    - `install/index`, the committed set (G445);
    - `install/r/<rid>/`, one record: `a/<path>` the selected variant's files; `m/manifest.cbor` and
      `m/manifest.cose`, the signed bytes as verified (`LgxPackage.signature` carries the second); `m/record.<g>`
      (G445);
    - `install/spool/`, the running operations' archives (5-5-3).
  - **`rid`** is 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits, 128 bits from the operating system's random source (`std/sysrand`),
    new for each record and never reused. It is random, not derived from the identity: a replacement needs a new
    directory while the old one is still committed; a crash leaves directories that nothing names; and a
    name-derived path would have to survive case folding and build metadata.
  - **Scope** (Q5 (a), the owner's answer of 2026-11-22): one inventory per Package Manager instance. A second store on the same
    root is refused by the lock (`sfInUse`), so that instance does not start: a shared mutable root is rejected, not
    served (PKG-0487). The deployment has no setting that shares a root, so PKG-0488's coherent sharing does not
    arise. DEPLOYMENT §1 says so.
  - **`local_path`** is absolute, `<state_dir>/install/r/<rid>/a/<path>`, because the Loader runs in logosd. The
    record file keeps it relative, and each load rebuilds it from the current state directory (G445). Over 4,096
    bytes fails admission (G452).
  - **Modes:** every directory 0700, `install/` included, and none made 0500; files 0400, none made executable and
    none rewritten (PKG-0499, PKG-0500). A 0500 directory would block the deletes G445 needs and adds nothing against
    the same user, who can change modes (D16). The Loader, as the same user, reads `local_path`, copies the library
    into its own private directory and never executes from the root.
  - **Path rules** (l.924, PKG-0489): `hostPathRules()` (case-insensitive on darwin, ios and windows), made
    case-insensitive when a probe at start finds that `lcn-probe` opens a `Lcn-probe` created in `install/`, as on a
    casefold directory, vfat or exFAT under Linux. Staging checks the variant's paths and every directory prefix
    under these rules (`checkInstallPaths`) before any write; a collision is `sfPaths`, whose outward code is
    5-5-4's (G449). Normalization needs no probe: LGX paths are NFC (G40), and two different NFC strings are never
    canonically equivalent.
  - **Resource access** (l.1182-1183, PKG-0498): a module reaches its packaged resources through its schema-typed
    configuration only. The handoff gives no package root and no artifact table (l.1185), and no artifact of a record
    is a path a module is told of. DEPLOYMENT §1 documents the convention.
  - **POSIX only**, as the hosted Package Manager's suites are: `pm/store.nim` and `pm/extract.nim` build on POSIX
    systems, and `test_pm_store` skips elsewhere.
- **Status:** built in part 5-5-2 (I121); the scope is Q5 (a), answered 2026-11-22.

### G445 — The installed-state store: the record file, the index and the commit
- **Kind:** IMPL (Tier 5 step 5-5; plan `tier5-plans/step5-5-plan.md` §4.2) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER l.778-787 (the
  record), l.814-822 (selected modules only, retention, one commitment per identity), l.1172 (the selected variant's
  artifacts only), l.1176 and l.1185 (verified-byte binding, a native library's installed path included), l.1302 (a
  failure leaves the installed set unchanged), l.1337-1341 (one edge per direct dependency, in declaration order),
  l.1721-1728 (serialization and durability).
- **Description:** the spec defines the record a caller sees, not how a Package Manager keeps it.
- **Decision:**
  - **The record file**, `install/r/<rid>/m/record.<g>` (`pm/installed.cddl`'s `lcn.pm_installed_record`):
    `format: 1`; `record`, the deterministic-CBOR bytes of the exact `installed_package_record`, its `local_path`s
    relative to the record's `a/` directory (the selected variant's artifact paths); `generation`, from 1; and
    `archive_digest`, the BLAKE3-256 of the archive it came from, for diagnostics only.
  - **Every load checks it** against that text, its `record` against App A's record rule, then against its signed
    manifest (`matchesManifest`): the same identity and commitment; the selected variant's artifacts exactly as
    signed; its selected module declarations unchanged and in manifest order; one edge per direct dependency, in
    order. The typed declarations kept are the manifest's.
  - **The index**, `install/index` (`lcn.pm_installed_index`): `format: 1`, `sequence` (commits so far) and one
    `{rid, generation, package, version}` per record, sorted by package name bytes, then version text bytes. Each
    identity and each rid occurs once; a rid is 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits. The identity is there so that a
    start can name a record whose file is missing or unreadable (R3). It is read and written within 64 MiB, which
    holds at least 200,000 records at the longest identities; an index that would pass it is refused.
  - **The schemas** both files are checked with (`installed.checkType`): `installed.cddl` on its own, as an
    ordinary supporting schema of the `lcn` namespace; and App A, which governs (PM l.1842-1845), with the manifest
    schema and the Module Configuration types it names (the latter from the Runtime Control types' supporting
    document, mirrored from `spec/mirrors/CFG/`), for the embedded record and each index identity
    (`package_identity`). App A's types are carried as bytes and text and checked apart, because one document's
    declarations share one namespace, and renaming `lcn.` rules into `logos.package_manager` would define `logos.`
    names of our own (BCP-0104). 5-5-1 first renamed them, as `test_pm_catalog` does in a test; `test_deployment`'s
    BCP-0104 scan of `src` caught it.
  - **The commit protocol** (`pm/store.nim`; l.1721-1728, PKG-0610, PKG-0611), under the storage failure model of
    DEPLOYMENT §19:
    1. **Stage** (`stage`): the paths under the root's rules (G444) and the admission bound (G452), both before any
       write; then the record's directory, `mkdirat` under the `install/r/` descriptor, written in full: `a/` (G446),
       then `m/manifest.cbor`, `m/manifest.cose` and `m/record.1`. A failure deletes the directory, which nothing
       names. A signer replacement (`stageSigner`) writes `m/record.<g+1>` in the committed directory and touches
       no artifact.
    2. **Sync, by the mode chosen at start** (`syncMode`):
       - `smSyncfs`, on Linux from 5.8 on ext4 (`f_type` 0xEF53): no per-file sync; one `syncfs` on the `install/r/`
         descriptor, opened at start and held for the store's life, so opened before any write it must cover
         (Fable's recheck, S5 condition 1). From 5.8 `syncfs` reports a write error anywhere on that filesystem
         since the descriptor last checked, so a write error of another module on the same filesystem fails our
         commit (S5 condition 2; DEPLOYMENT §19). sync(2) on server.lan (Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.8) says both:
         `syncfs` gives what an `fsync` of every file of the filesystem gives, and from 5.8 it reports an inode that
         failed to be written back. The gain was measured on ext4 (plan "Spikes": 45 ms against 1,164 ms for 3,000 files), so
         other Linux filesystems, and kernels before 5.8, take the other mode.
       - `smEachFile`, everywhere else: each file before it is closed, then each directory made below `a/`,
         deepest first, then `a/`, `m/`, the record's directory and `install/r/`, each with a plain `fsync`
         (`extract.fsyncOnly`). On
         Darwin that moves the data to the drive; the drive's flush is the `F_FULLFSYNC` that `writeAtomic` issues
         on the new index before its rename (`durable.nim`), which flushes the whole drive cache and so covers
         every file synced before it. No other `F_FULLFSYNC` is issued (S1).
    3. **Commit** (`commit(add, drop)`): one `writeAtomic` of `install/index`, with `sequence` one higher. One commit
       adds records, drops rids and names regenerated records; an identity staged while another record of it is
       committed is `sfConflict` (PKG-0182: one commitment per identity). A `writeAtomic` failure leaves the store
       refusing every later staging and commit until a restart, since only a start knows which index is in place.
    4. The caller swaps its snapshot and answers (5-5-4).
  - **What each mutation writes in its one index replace:** install adds one rid; remove drops one; update drops the
    current rid and adds the target's (PKG-0408); a same-commitment update drops the current rid only (PKG-0537); a
    signer replacement names `m/record.<g+1>` (PKG-0608). A crash before step 3's rename leaves the old state; after
    it, the new state with unnamed directories (PKG-0611).
  - **`durable.nim` is unchanged**, against plan §5.2 (Fable's S1 allowed either): `fsyncOnly` and `syncFs` are in
    `pm/extract.nim`, and `durable.nim`, which 65 suites reach, keeps its `syncFd`.
  - **The start** (`openStore`, before the instance is ready):
    1. the lock, then the probe (G444);
    2. **no index:** an empty or absent `r/` is a fresh root, and an empty index is written; an `r/` that holds
       entries is damage (`sfDamaged`, S6): the start stops, the error names the root, and nothing is deleted;
    3. **an index:** read within 64 MiB and checked; each named record loaded and checked as above, its `local_path`s
       rebuilt under the current state directory, and its admission bound checked again at that path (PKG-0471).
       Any failure stops the start, naming the identity from the index (R3); nothing is skipped. A module whose
       configuration artifact no longer matches its signed digest cannot be handed off until its package is
       installed again (R4), so its handoff is not required at start; that is a note for the operator's log, not a
       failure, and the instance starts so that the repair can run;
    4. only then is what no committed record names deleted: other record directories, other generations, `*.tmp`
       and `spool/`, since nothing runs yet. Each deletion and each failure to delete is a note (`notes`).
    5. Artifacts are not hashed again at start; the retained check runs at use (G448).
  - **Retirement** (R1): a directory or a record generation that the new index no longer names is retired with the
    sequence of the commit that retired it. `collect(oldestHeld)` deletes what was retired at or before the oldest
    sequence still held, and keeps for the next collect what it cannot delete.
    - **The invariant** (Fable's recheck, R1.1): one worker runs the store's calls, jobs in order, and a deletion is
      queued only after the release of the last holder that could see the item, so no delete runs under a reader.
      The worker and the holders are 5-5-3's and 5-5-4's.
    - **Only holders that read files count** (R1.2): an operation, a handoff under construction, a retained check.
      A list cursor holds decoded records, not files, and must not keep directories alive.
    - The cost is disk held while an old snapshot lives, which at the maxima can be a long sliced resolution.
  - **Binding** (PKG-0181, PKG-0293, PKG-0500; TXT-0472): the bytes are retained while the record is named; files are
    0400 inside 0700 directories; nothing in the Package Manager rewrites a committed file; a replacement is always a
    new directory through the full acceptance path. `checkRetained` hashes each artifact of a record, opened below
    `a/` with no link followed at any component, against its signed digest; a change, a removal or a link is
    `sfIntegrity` (`artifact-integrity-failed`). A packaged native library is one of those artifacts, so the binding
    holds for its installed path (l.1185). The Loader hashes its own copy against the handoff's signed hash.
  - **A damaged record and its repair** (R4): once retained bytes change, every operation that reaches the record
    fails `artifact-integrity-failed` and leaves the installed set unchanged (l.1302). An install of the same
    commitment reaches it too, so it does not repair it; a remove does not resolve, so it does not hash, but it is
    refused while a dependent exists. The repair is: remove the dependents, then the package, then install them
    again. DEPLOYMENT §19 says so. logos-lips `45e526a3` (Fable's editorial remark) asks the spec for a shorter path;
    it stops nothing.
  - **Test hooks** (`-d:lcnTestHooks` only): `crashAt` stops a staging or a commit where a crash would (after the
    files, after `index.tmp`, after the rename); `admission.admissionLimitForTests` lowers the admission bound so
    that `test_pm_store` reaches PKG-0471's edge without 16 MiB of record.
- **Status:** the files built in part 5-5-1, the store in part 5-5-2 (I121).

### G446 — Extraction, the spool and the reader
- **Kind:** IMPL (Tier 5 step 5-5; plan §4.3 and §4.3a; the spool is the owner's Q2 (d), the reader Q4 (b), both answered
  2026-11-22) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER
  l.926-933 (the destination stays inside the root), l.963 (every regular file of the selected variant), l.1094
  (could not be materialized), §14 (`artifact-integrity-failed`: escaped their realization root).
- **Decision (the writing half, 5-5-2):**
  - **Descriptor-relative** (`pm/extract.nim`; PKG-0204, PKG-0274): every name is created relative to a directory
    descriptor this extraction opened, never through a path. The record directory is made with `mkdirat` under the
    `install/r/` descriptor; each directory component with `mkdirat` (0700), then opened
    `O_DIRECTORY | O_NOFOLLOW` relative to its parent; each file created
    `O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC`, 0400, and written in 1 MiB chunks. The components are
    ones the reader has checked: no `..`, no `.`, no empty segment, NFC (G40). So no component that is a link is
    followed, nothing outside the record's directory is named, and the destination stays within the root by
    construction.
  - **An existing name**, a planted link or a collision the probe missed fails `O_EXCL`, `O_NOFOLLOW` or `mkdirat`
    (`efExists`, the store's `sfEscaped`): `artifact-integrity-failed`, "escaped their realization root". A write
    that fails for room or I/O (`efWrite`, `sfWrite`) is `package-unavailable` (PKG-0271, l.1094). The directory is
    deleted at once, or at the next start; the outward codes are 5-5-4's.
  - **What is written:** the selected variant's declared artifacts, which are every regular file of it (l.963); no
    directory entry, no other variant; nothing executed, built or scripted (PKG-0011, PKG-0192, PKG-0499). The
    Runtime and the Loader see a `local_path` only after the commit (PKG-0012, PKG-0219, PKG-0292).
  - **Few descriptors:** directories are reopened per file and closed, so a variant of 65,536 files holds no more
    than its depth open.
  - **The stop flag** (W2) is checked between chunks and between files; a stop is `sfStopped`, and the directory is
    deleted.
  - **Reads below a record** (`hashBelow`, `readBelow`, the handoff's `reader`): each component opened relative to
    its parent with `O_NOFOLLOW`, the last a regular file; the handoff's reads are capped at 8 MiB, the largest
    configuration artifact.
  - **What it costs** (the Mac, orc, a scratch program; one package of 20,000 small artifacts, near the size
    PKG-0471's test first used): building the archive 16.6 s, `openLgx` 17.4 s, `decodeManifest` 2.0 s, `stage`
    10.1 s (20,000 files, each `fsync`ed), `commit` 26 ms, `openStore` 15.5 s (one record's load and check:
    decoding, `matchesManifest`, the admission bound; not measured apart) and deleting the record 5.0 s. The reader
    is 5-5-2b's; the start's cost per record goes to CONFORMANCE with 5-5-4.
- **The spool** (Q2 (d), with the details of plan §4.3: the root's archive never evicted, ineligible archives
  first, the inspections' share bounded, a package's file deleted after its commit) is part 5-5-3. **The streaming
  reader** (Q4 (b): the owner, "I want the streaming reader there"; plan §4.3a) is part 5-5-2b, which builds after
  Fable's check of §4.3a and planning's go. It replaces the ranges change of draft 2.
- **Status:** the writing half built in part 5-5-2 (I121).

### G450 — The Package Manager's responses and messages
- **Kind:** IMPL (Tier 5 step 5-5; plan §4.7) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER l.1467-1470 (a success variant holds no
  error, an error variant exactly one), l.1471-1490 (`package_error`), l.1493 (`invalid-request`), l.1512-1517
  (messages; package errors are not authorization decisions; invocation failures are never package errors), §15's
  response types.
- **Decision:**
  - **`pm/responses.nim`** (the plan's `results.nim`: that name is the `results` package's, which every module
    imports) has one encoder per §15 response variant: `{installed}` for install and update, `{}` for remove,
    `{inspection}`, `{handoff}`, the installed-list page `{packages, ?next_cursor}`, and `{error: package_error}`.
    Each builds deterministic CBOR from typed values. `test_pm_records` checks each against App A's response types,
    and every error code against every method's response.
  - **A message** is the caller's public text, cut to 512 bytes at a UTF-8 boundary. It names only the request's
    own fields, identities and versions the caller named or may observe, and a fixed cause; never a state
    directory, `local_path`, binding or storage name, locator, trust content or limit value. A handoff refusal keeps
    what a read reported, which may name a path, in `detail`, for the operator's log only. The check of every
    operation's messages against a sentinel state directory and binding comes with 5-5-4.
  - **Invocation failures:** `moduleError()` is `MODULE_ERROR` with no message and no detail. A package error is an
    operational result in a successful response (PKG-0361). The admission bound, a damaged installed state, a worker
    failure and a stop are invocation failures, never package errors (PKG-0362).
  - **`invalid-request`** is used only for a request that would fail unchanged again (PKG-0359): today, the handoff
    of a module the record does not select.
- **Status:** built in part 5-5-1 (I121).

### G451 — The handoff's construction, and package configuration at inspection (PKG-0060)
- **Kind:** Reading and IMPL (Tier 5 step 5-5; plan §4.8; planning's ruling Q-P1 (a), 2026-11-22) · **Specs:**
  PACKAGE MANAGER l.362-364 (artifacts verified before parsing; the five `invalid-package` cases), l.539 (the
  retained signer), l.1386-1449 (the handoff).
- **Decision:**
  - **`pm/handoff.nim`'s `buildHandoff(record, base, manifest, commitment, module, trust, read)`** builds
    `runtime_handoff` for one selected module: the retained signer (PKG-0438); `module`, the flat name (PKG-0348);
    the record's identity, and the implementation artifact's id and `local_path` (PKG-0340); its hash as signed, with
    the suite the manifest commitment names, whatever the file holds now (PKG-0341: the Loader hashes its own copy);
    the exact manifest commitment (PKG-0339); `primary_contract`, `implements`, `extends`, `requires` and
    `requested_permissions` copied from the signed declaration when present, and never added (G391's construction);
    and the configuration declaration. `read` is the worker's read in the engine and an archive's verified entry at
    admission.
  - **The configuration declaration** (`resolveConfiguration`; PKG-0342 to 0344): the schema artifact's bytes,
    checked against the signed digest, as UTF-8 text of 1 to 1,048,576 bytes (checked before anything parses it);
    the root and live support copied; the declared document commitment's fields copied, with the subtree root
    derived for the root; `default_value` only when a default artifact is declared, its bytes checked against the
    signed digest; then `runtime/configcheck.acceptConfiguration`, which recomputes both roots and checks the
    default as one complete value of the root. No artifact id or path is carried.
  - **Refusals are typed**, and 5-6a maps them for `get_runtime_handoff`:

    | Refusal | Code |
    |---|---|
    | not installed | `package-not-installed` |
    | a module the record does not select | `invalid-request` |
    | the retained signer not accepted by active trust (PKG-0341, PKG-0080) | `signature-verification-failed` |
    | a schema or default artifact absent or changed | `artifact-integrity-failed` |
    | the configuration not accepted | `invalid-package` |
    | the record differs from its signed manifest (a widened declaration) | none: `MODULE_ERROR` (G450) |

  - **PKG-0060 at inspection:** `checkConfigurations` builds the same declaration from the selected variant's
    verified entries, in `vcache.inspect` after `openLgx`, so last in G29/P7a order. Each failure is
    `invalid-package`: invalid CDDL, a document commitment mismatch, an absent or invalid root, an unresolved
    non-common reference, an invalid default. Only the selected variant's selected modules are checked. The check is
    in `pm/`, not `package/lgx.nim`; the layer lint passes with `runtime/configcheck` in the Package Manager's
    closure. No fixture of 5-3b's carries a configuration, so no earlier result changes.
  - **Units:** PKG-0060, 0337, 0339 to 0344, 0348 and 0438 are claimed here. PKG-0338, 0347 and 0351 are built here
    and stay 5-8's (G391); PKG-0345, 0346, 0349 and 0350 are 5-8's.
  - **A returned handoff holds no files** (Fable's recheck of draft 2, R1.3). The Loader reads `local_path` later,
    in logosd. A remove or an update that commits in between can retire and delete the record's directory first
    (G445's deferred deletion counts only holders inside the Package Manager). That load then fails, and a new
    handoff, from the record installed then, succeeds. 5-6a and 5-8 must not read that failure as damage.
- **Status:** built in part 5-5-1 (I121).

### G452 — The admission bound
- **Kind:** IMPL (Tier 5 step 5-5; plan §4.9) · **Specs:** PACKAGE MANAGER l.824-830 (every complete required
  single-record result fits the 16 MiB Transport body; which results; surrounding fields count; `MODULE_ERROR` with
  no detail; kept on restore and on changed paths; a larger Transport limit relaxes nothing).
- **Decision:**
  - **`pm/admission.nim`'s `admits(record, base, handoffs)`** encodes each required result in its real Transport
    response envelope with `transport/envelope.encodeMessage`, nothing estimated: `{installed: R}` (install and
    update alike); the page `{packages: [R], next_cursor: C}` with a 512-byte cursor; and `{handoff: H}` for each
    selected module, its schema and default included. Each envelope carries the largest call id, 2^64−1, and a
    payload commitment of two 32-byte roots. Each body must be at most `MinFrameLimit` (`transport/framing.nim`),
    the Core-owned 16 MiB, never the configured limit. Each value must also be valid under App A, so a `local_path`
    over 4,096 bytes fails here.
  - **The envelope adds 134 bytes** around an empty result; `test_pm_records` pins it, and shows the page at exactly
    16 MiB passing and one byte more failing, and the install result failing when it is the one over.
  - **A handoff from a legal package cannot fail it today:** a manifest is at most 4 MiB, a schema document 1 MiB and
    a default 8 MiB, so a handoff stays under 14 MiB. It is checked all the same; the test makes one fail with a long
    `implements` list that App A allows.
  - **A failure** is an `AdmissionFault`, which names the result for the operator's log; outward it is
    `MODULE_ERROR` with no detail (`responses.moduleError`). Before any write it fails the operation (5-5-4, PKG-0470);
    at start the instance does not start, and the record is named (5-5-2, PKG-0471).
- **Status:** built in part 5-5-1 (I121).
