### G335 — The thread-confined module kit
- **Kind:** READING + IMPL · **Specs:** INTERFACE §2.6-§2.8 (l.1894, l.1904, l.1924-1928, l.1942-1947,
  l.1949-1962), §2.9; TIER5-PLAN N-1, §7 A7; plan `tier5-plans/stepN-1-kit.md` §3.1, P3-P5.
- **Reading.** A provider entry may hand its work to another thread while the caller waits: the
  entry's obligations (its result, the per-thread diagnostic lifetime, the invocation borrow) are met
  on the calling thread, and l.1904's "the thread that called" is the thread the Runtime called. A
  provider may serialize its instance's work on one thread of its own (l.1942-1947 leave the
  provider's threading to it), provided a call made on that thread itself never waits for that thread
  (l.1928).
- **Decision.** `lcn-gen kit --confined` generates a kit over `codegen/confinedrt`, reached through the
  `logos_sdk/confined` facade (`logos_sdk/kit`, `confinedrt`, `base/hostsignals` and chronos). Each
  context has one **module thread**, made by the library's own runtime, which runs a chronos
  dispatcher: the instance is allocated, used and released there only, so under refc its handlers may
  keep GC'd values in it (lifting I71's limit for such modules, G342). `_MODULE_init`, `_destroy`,
  `_dispatch`, `_apply_configuration` and the typed `_CALL_` functions build a job on the caller's
  stack, queue it and wait on the job's own condition; the module thread writes the outcome into the
  job's fixed storage and the caller builds the `logos_result_t` on its own thread. `_name`,
  `_call_surface` and `_free` stay on the caller. One chronos task per job, so an `async` handler that
  awaits lets the thread serve the next job. An entry called on the module thread itself runs inline,
  polling the dispatcher until it is done; `confinedrt` refuses to compile under
  `chronosStrictReentrancy`, which forbids that nested poll. **Serving waits (P3):** every wait of the
  module thread on another kit thread polls the dispatcher, so a job that arrives meanwhile runs.
  `post` / `lcn_kit_post` hand a C callback to the module thread from any thread, one no Nim runtime has
  seen included, without the Nim heap. **Destroy:** `destroyModule` and the release run on the module
  thread, the publisher thread delivers what was queued and exits, the module thread answers what is
  left NOT_READY and tears down its dispatcher, both threads are joined; a failed initialization joins
  them the same way, dropping queued events. What still runs while `destroyModule` runs is G437 (N-1e).
  **The host's SIGPIPE (P5, G340):** confined kit libraries
  are built with `--import:logos_sdk/base/hostsignals` and the generated export template restores the
  disposition last.
- **Tests:** `sdk/tests/test_kit_confined.nim` (in process, all three builds): every entry kind handed
  off, 16 threads, P3, P4, inline nesting, foreign posts, init failure, destroy with queued events, 100
  create and destroy cycles and the descriptor count. `sdk/tests/test_kit_dylib.nim`: a library whose
  main module imports chronos first leaves SIGPIPE as it was. `tests/test_kit_mixed.nim` (G342).
- **Status:** built 2026-11-20 (N-1 sub-part 3; I101); `_MODULE_async_api` built with G338 (sub-part 4).

### G336 — The invocation context of a confined kit
- **Kind:** READING · **Specs:** INTERFACE §2.9.2 (l.2125-2137), l.2150-2161; claude-spec-comments-3
  TF-03 (third point).
- **Reading.** The module thread acting for a blocked entry is not an "unrelated thread" (l.2129): the
  context the entry captured is borrowed for that job, and its operations may run on any thread while
  the borrow is held (l.2134).
- **Decision.** The entry captures `current()` on its own thread before handing off; the module thread
  uses it for that job only. A plain handler reaches it through a per-thread **confined scope**
  (`kitrt`), set only while its synchronous segment runs and saved, cleared and restored around every
  nested poll and serving wait (P4), so a task resumed inside a nested poll never sees another job's
  context. An `async` handler takes `inv: Invocation` as its third parameter; inside an async task the
  per-thread API answers NOT_READY, and an `Invocation` refuses use (NOT_READY) once its job has ended
  (l.2130). An inline entry pushes its context and restores the outer one (l.2128). Before an entry
  returns, every operation of its job has finished, its scoped publications included; the Runtime's
  `execution_release` still never waits (l.2137).
- **Tests:** `sdk/tests/test_kit_confined.nim` "invocation context": interleaved async handlers each see
  their own caller; NOT_READY in an async task; an `Invocation` kept past its job; nesting.
- **Amended (N-1 sub-part 4, G338):** a deferred job has no entry thread and no captured context: it
  uses its invocation's own (l.2121-2124), through the confined scope or `inv`, until it completes, and
  a plain handler's `publishScoped` in it goes to the publisher thread.
- **Status:** built 2026-11-20 (N-1 sub-part 3; I101).

### G337 — Publication from a confined kit
- **Kind:** IMPL · **Specs:** INTERFACE l.1918-1928, l.2150-2161, l.3351, Appendix A.4 (l.4115);
  RUNTIME l.1200.
- **Decision.** `publish` (instance-wide) checks the event as the callback will, copies it into C
  memory and queues it for the context's **publisher thread**, which calls the publish callback in
  order. It returns the kit's check, or the kit's own NOT_READY when the queue is full (64 events or
  1 MiB [IMPL]). **This departs from Appendix A.4**, whose helper returns the callback's result: waiting
  for the callback would stop the module thread from serving a subscriber that re-enters from the
  publisher thread, the re-entry IFC-0281/0282 are claimed for. The callback's refusals are plain API
  (`publishRefusals`, `lastPublishRefusal`). `publishAsync` returns a future of the callback's result
  and waits for room. A plain handler's `publishScoped` is handed to the entry thread, which holds the
  provider entry, while the module thread serves (P3); an async handler's goes through the publisher
  thread with its invocation's context. A failure's message and detail are copied on the thread that
  ran the context's `publish` (l.2161). Before an entry returns, its scoped events are drained (R
  l.1200). Destroy delivers what was queued, then joins. Every copy is zeroed after its last use (G276).
- **For the guide:** `publish` is queued, so an event can reach subscribers after the handler's
  response, and OK is not acceptance; await `publishAsync` where the order matters.
- **Tests:** `sdk/tests/test_kit_confined.nim` "publication": re-entry during each publication path
  from the publisher and the entry thread, plain and async; refusals; a full queue; the drain rule.
  `tests/test_kit_mixed.nim` MX-1, MX-2 (G342).
- **Status:** built 2026-11-20 (N-1 sub-part 3; I101).

### G338 — The deferred provider of a confined kit (`_MODULE_async_api`) and `invokeAsync`
- **Kind:** IMPL · **Specs:** INTERFACE §2.9.1 (l.2043), §2.9.2 (l.2058-2117), §2.9.3 (l.2119-2137),
  §5.2; TRANSPORT l.841-843; TIER5-PLAN N-1; plan `tier5-plans/stepN-1-kit.md` §3.2.
- **Decision.** `lcn-gen kit --confined --async-api` (refused without `--confined`, and for a kit with
  no provider) adds `logos_<m>_MODULE_async_api`, which returns the address of one static, immutable
  descriptor (`submit`, `request_cancel`, the provider ABI version and its extent) and touches no
  context. Its symbol joins the export lists (G341). In `codegen/confinedrt`:
  - **`submit`** copies nothing the Runtime lends (method, request bytes and context stay borrowed until
    the release, l.2079-2081). A null or malformed invocation (version, extent, a null `complete` or
    `execution_release`) stops the process, since it cannot be answered; a null module or a method or
    request the invocation check refuses completes MODULE_ERROR at once. Otherwise the job is allocated
    in C memory, linked among the context's outstanding invocations under its lock, queued and the
    module thread woken, and `submit` returns; while the context is being destroyed the invocation
    completes NOT_READY instead.
  - **On the module thread** the job runs the route `_MODULE_dispatch` runs (shared provider logic,
    l.2072), over the borrowed bytes, with the invocation's own context: a plain handler sees it
    through the confined scope (G336), an `async` handler as `inv`. No instance answers NOT_READY; a
    cancellation that arrived while the job was queued answers CANCELLED without the handler. The
    handler's future is recorded on the job while it runs and awaited shielded (`noCancel(join)`), so
    its cancellation never cancels the job: a cancelled future answers CANCELLED "the handler was
    cancelled", and a handler that catches `CancelledError` answers what it returns.
  - **Scoped publications.** No entry thread waits for a deferred job, so a plain handler's
    `publishScoped` goes to the publisher thread with the invocation's context while the module thread
    serves (P3), as an async handler's does (G337). The job completes only after every publication of
    its invocation was answered (RUNTIME l.1200).
  - **Completion** (l.2085-2091). The failure is normalized as on the synchronous path (clipped,
    checked, no NUL; `kitrt.normalizedFailure`, shared with `failureResult`); a success with no bytes,
    which no route makes, is MODULE_ERROR. The response, or the failure's NUL-terminated message and
    its detail, go into one C block whose owner zeroes and frees it on any thread (G276); out of memory,
    the code goes without diagnostics. The job leaves the outstanding list, its `Invocation` stops
    admitting operations (l.2136), then `complete` runs once and `execution_release` once.
  - **`request_cancel`** finds the invocation by address among the context's outstanding ones under the
    lock and returns when it is not there (l.2105-2108). Otherwise it marks it and, unless a notice is
    queued already or the context is closed, queues one notice, which holds its own reference to the
    job's memory; it never waits (l.2111). On the module thread the notice calls `cancelSoon` on the
    handler's future while it runs; a plain handler sees `isCancelled`.
  - **Destroy.** The Runtime drains invocations before destroy (l.2114). For one that does not, the
    teardown completes each queued and each outstanding invocation NOT_READY "the module was destroyed",
    once. The drain never needs `_MODULE_destroy`: the module thread runs on its own (l.2115).
  - **Amended 2026-11-21 (stepN-1c, CI run 44888184613; Fable's review):** with a conforming Runtime
    nothing changes. The drain never needs `_MODULE_destroy` (l.2115), and the Runtime's own drain
    tests still assert that its cancellation came before destroy.
    - For a Runtime that destroys with submitted invocations outstanding, `_MODULE_destroy` now stops
      that residual work (l.2100) before the author's `destroyModule`. First every new job answers
      NOT_READY (the instance is detached; `disposed`, which drops posted tasks, is set only after).
      **See G437 (N-1e):** `disposed` is now set only once `destroyModule`'s future has finished,
      and events and end reports are dropped from the start of destroy.
      Then each waiting `async` handler's future is cancelled as `request_cancel` would, and the kit
      awaits up to 2 s (`UnwindMs`, fixed) for the outstanding invocations while the instance still
      lives. The wait is an `await`, never a nested poll, since destroy may run inside a handler's
      nested loop.
    - A handler destroy cancelled completes NOT_READY whatever it answers, its outcome wiped. One
      waiting for its scoped publications completes with its own outcome.
    - What is still outstanding (a handler that ignores the cancellation) is completed NOT_READY at
      teardown and its task abandoned. chronos pins a waiting async frame (`futureContinue`'s
      `GC_ref`, released only when the awaited future finishes), so the frames, the instance they
      hold and the request they decoded stay for the life of the process. That is the conforming
      outcome for work that cannot quiesce (l.2116-2117).
    - Before this, every such task was abandoned. LeakSanitizer reported it from `[IFC-0769]` on
      both Linux architectures, 3322 bytes in 35 indirect allocations (CI run 44888184613; the
      x86_64 job ran on to its time limit and showed as cancelled), and again on framework.lan
      (x86_64) over 109f4d8. A handler whose await ended between destroy's return and teardown
      also resumed after `destroyModule`.
    - With this, `test_kit_confined` under ASan reports no leak on framework.lan. Run there with
      the `noCancel` case not skipped, LeakSanitizer reports 3258 bytes in 35 indirect
      allocations, all from that case's `wait` 11: the residue above, and why that case skips
      under ASan.
    - Now a handler that honours the cancellation resumes only to unwind it, before
      `destroyModule`. No task resumes after teardown, but one may still resume before it in two
      cases this does not cover: the inner job of an inline re-entry, and synchronous entries still
      running. The inner job is a `ConfinedJob`, not in the outstanding list, so nothing cancels it;
      destroy then waits for it without a bound, and its handlers run after `destroyModule`, as
      before.
    - Not done: `isCancelled` answering true for plain handlers once destroy has begun (optional).
    - Not checked: whether a generated route wipes a marked decoded request and response on the
      cancellation path, now destroy's usual way out (a W-case).
    - Tests in `test_kit_confined`. `[IFC-0769]` asserts that the destroyed instance is freed (orc).
      A new case, a handler under `noCancel`, asserts NOT_READY once, destroy returning after the
      bound, and the instance kept. It does not run under ASan, which would report the residue. The
      ledger fixture's instance counts its frees (`freed`), and `wait` 11 sleeps under `noCancel`.
- **`invokeAsync`** (`codegen/confinedcalls`, behind the `logos_sdk/confined` facade): a typed call
  through a handle the kit wrapped (G339), as a chronos future of its outcome, on its module thread;
  any other use answers NOT_READY at once. A generic over the generated `prepareInvoke`, it submits at
  once; the completion runs on the module thread and completes the future, and the call is released
  after the completion returned (l.2043). Cancelling the future (an awaiting handler's cancellation
  reaching it) asks the call's cancellation; the future completes with the call's outcome, a nonzero
  `timeoutMs` being its deadline (TIMEOUT).
- **Reading.** l.2112 (IFC-0767, a SHOULD): the kit's own backend work is the handler's future, which it
  cancels; cancelling the author's backend work is the author's (the unit stays out of scope, with
  IFC-0758).
- **Hosted.** In a Module Host, a consumer's Cancel that reaches the host before the Runtime's verdict
  ends the Request there and its handler never runs (`host/endpoint` `endedBySession`); MX-4 waits for
  the handler to run before it cancels.
- **For the guide:** an async handler is cancelled at its `await` (`CancelledError`): catch it to
  clean up and answer, or let it pass and the kit answers CANCELLED. Use `invokeAsync` in confined
  mode rather than a blocking `invoke`. `--async-api` lets a long delayed Response run without holding
  a host call slot (G100).
- **Tests:** `sdk/tests/test_kit_confined.nim` "the deferred provider" (12 cases, orc, refc and
  orc-release): the descriptor from every thread; one answer through `submit` and `_MODULE_dispatch`;
  `submit` and `request_cancel` while the module thread is busy; a cancellation an async handler
  observes; hooks racing 64 completions from 4 threads; the owner's regions until cleared on another
  thread; no use after the release; scoped publications with a re-entering subscriber; destroy with an
  invocation outstanding, cancelled and unwound or abandoned after the bound (2026-11-21); `invokeAsync`'s completion, deadline and cancellation, and its NOT_READY off
  the module thread. `sdk/tests/test_kit_dylib.nim`: the confined sensor library's typed, dispatch and
  deferred surfaces give one answer, the implemented interface's method included; its export list.
  `tests/test_kit_mixed.nim` MX-4: prepared calls to the ledger's deferred surface through the Runtime,
  `direct_dynamic` and hosted: a completion, a cancellation that reaches its async handler, a deadline.
  The regenerated ledger kit and the new confined sensor kit (`sdk/tests/generated/confined/`).
- **Status:** built 2026-11-20 (N-1 sub-part 4; I101).

### G339 — lcn-gen's consumer helpers and interface-only provider kits
- **Kind:** IMPL · **Specs:** INTERFACE §2.5 (l.1393-1489: subscriptions, `observe_end`,
  `observe_subscription_end`, the typed event helper of l.1489), §2.8 (l.1934-1940), §2.9.1
  (l.1992-2052), §5.2; RUNTIME §9.3 (l.3017-3082); TIER5-PLAN N-1.
- **Runtime modules**, so that generated code never reaches the Runtime Control types and a plain
  module never reaches chronos: `logos_sdk/codegen/consumert.nim`, which every generated
  `<stem>_calls.nim` imports beside `invokert`; `codegen/handover.nim` (what crosses to a confined
  kit's module thread, chronos-free); and `logos_sdk/kit/routes.nim`, for module code.
  `tools/lint/layers.toml`'s `kit_facade` lists the roots generated code imports (`kit.nim`,
  `codegen/invokert.nim`, `codegen/consumert.nim`), and the lint fails if any of them reaches `rcclient`
  or `rc_types` (`kit-facade`, also for the `confined_facade` root `confined.nim`) or anything in their
  closure imports chronos (`kit-chronos`).
- **Wrapped handles (`consumert`).** `wrapRoute(handle, onRouteEnd, user)` takes ownership of a
  materialized handle and registers `observe_end` and `observe_subscription_end` once each, before any
  subscription. A termination code from either registration fails the wrap with that code (l.1459), as
  INVALID_PARAMS (a raw registration came first) and MODULE_ERROR (capacity) do; the handle is released.
  A route's end goes to `onRouteEnd` alone (l.1474), and a binding-ended subscription to its `onEnd`
  with NOT_AUTHORISED or MODULE_ERROR (l.1479). Generated per event:
  `subscribe(route, <Event>, onEvent, onEnd, onInvalid, user)`, each delivery decoded with the event's
  checked decoder, one that does not decode going to `onInvalid`. The subscription's state is linked
  before the binding's `subscribe` is called (l.1395, l.1398). Generated per method: `invoke(route,
  <Request>)` under the handle's rules, and `prepareInvoke(route, <Request>, onDone, user, timeoutMs)`,
  a prepared call with a typed completion: options and callbacks are always passed (l.1992), a nonzero
  `timeoutMs` is the call's deadline (TIMEOUT, l.2020, l.2024), the response owner is released after the
  decode on every path (l.2052), and `release` from the call's own completion is NOT_READY (l.2043).
- **Marked payloads (G276).** `prepareInvoke` wipes the request's tree and bytes once the binding has
  them. For a method whose response `_sensitive` marks, it passes `marked = true`, and the decoded
  response is erased (`wipeTyped`) once `onDone` returns: `onDone` copies what it keeps. The decode
  path reads the error with `unsafeError`, since results 0.5.1's `isOkOr` and `valueOr` copy the whole
  result, a marked value included. `_sensitive` marks method payloads only (INTERFACE §1.2.1), so an
  event delivery is never erased.
- **The handler rule, by thread.** The handle counts, per thread, its handlers and end callbacks that
  are running. An operation on the handle from such a thread is NOT_READY (l.1939), except the running
  handler's own unsubscription, which takes no lock (l.1937-1938); so is `release` (l.1485). The check
  comes before the handle's operation lock, so a handler nested in its own handle's call (l.1405) is
  refused rather than deadlocked. Operations from other threads wait on that lock (l.1935). End
  callbacks take no lock an operation holds (l.1467). A prepared call's `submit`, `cancel` and `release`
  take no handle lock (l.2001-2004), so a completion inline in `submit` may prepare the next call.
- **Lifetimes.** What a binding thread reads is C-allocated shared memory with `{.nimcall.}` procedure
  pointers. A subscription's state is freed by whichever comes last, its unsubscription or its last
  running frame; frames are counted under the owner's state lock, so an end report that runs while an
  external unsubscription returns (which waits for handlers only, l.1416-1419) keeps valid state. Each
  callback starts with `kitrt.callbackEnter`, which registers its thread with the library's Nim runtime
  as an exported entry's `kitEnter` does (I71), without clearing the thread's last failure, since a
  callback can run nested inside an entry. Under refc a handler still must not store GC'd values (I71).
- **Runtime Control subscriptions.** `consumert.BindingEvents` gives the same typed subscriptions over
  a module's binding (l.3868). The first registers the binding's `observe_subscription_end` once, under
  a lock (l.1476-1477); a raw registration made before makes it fail INVALID_PARAMS. Inside that end
  callback every operation of these helpers through the binding is refused NOT_READY (l.1480);
  `insideBindingEnd` tells other code the same.
- **Routes (`kit/routes`).** A `RouteSet` belongs to one module instance and its binding. It holds the
  route handles and prepared calls given to it and its Runtime Control subscriptions; `close` releases
  the calls, then the handles, then unsubscribes the subscriptions, in `_MODULE_destroy` (l.1959-1960)
  and before a failed `_MODULE_init` returns (l.1607, l.3892). After a failed initialization the
  binding's end registration's state is kept, on a list that keeps it reachable, since the Runtime
  suppresses those callbacks only before `_MODULE_destroy` (l.1954). `openRoute(set, root, schema,
  access, cardinality, provider, requestKey, onRouteEnd, user)` calls `establish_route` with a fresh
  `request_key` (128 random bits) unless one is given, so a retry replays (R l.3072-3080); continuations
  or a route that is not ready from the module's own binding are a Runtime fault, MODULE_ERROR, before
  anything is materialized (R l.3019-3020); `partial` is returned as it is (R l.3047). Each route is
  materialized and wrapped with its own outcome, and its record is returned without its invocation.
  `materialize` (after a `renewRoute` of a replayed route, R l.3080-3081), `renewRoute` (a fresh key
  unless given) and `closeRoute` (`close_route` takes no key) complete it; `subscribe(set, eventId,
  <Event>, …)` takes a Runtime Control event by its schema event identifier. `rcclient.prepareBytes`
  and `prepare` take the same `timeoutMs`.
- **Confined mode (sub-part 3).** One calls file serves both modes: a handle, a binding's
  subscriptions and a prepared call carry an optional **dispatcher** (P2), a context pointer and one C
  function that queues a task node for a confined kit's module thread. Module code passes the kit's
  (`services.dispatcher`) to `wrapRoute`, `newBindingEvents` or `newRouteSet(services)`. With one,
  handlers, end reports and completions run on the module thread, never in the delivery: a delivery is
  copied into C memory on the delivering thread and decoded on the module thread; a delivery whose
  callback runs on the module thread itself is queued too, never run inline; end reports and
  completions use task nodes reserved in the subscription, the handle and the call, so they are never
  refused. A completion's status, message, detail and response bytes are copied and its response owner
  cleared on the delivering thread (l.2052); `CompleteProc` takes the status already read. **The queue
  is bounded (P1)**, per context, 1024 events [IMPL] (`setDeliveryBound` lowers it in tests): a delivery
  that finds it full ends its subscription from inside its own delivery, a self-unsubscription that never
  waits (l.1424-1426), drops the event and reports `onEnd(MODULE_ERROR)` on the module thread after the
  queued events, as a binding does at its bound (l.1473, l.1479); a later `unsubscribe` is OK without a
  second binding call. An unsubscription or release by the module thread is external (l.1416-1419,
  l.1434): the subscription or handle is marked closing first, so a delivery still running drops its
  event, and its memory is freed by the last task that names it. A call released before its queued
  completion runs never completes. Tasks still queued at destroy are dropped, freeing and erasing what
  they hold. `invokeAsync`, a future over `prepareInvoke` on the module thread, is G338.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_consumert.nim` (in process, 19 cases): typed delivery and unsubscribe; the
  handler rule; a handler nested in its own handle's call; an end report while an operation holds the
  lock; a subscription ended at the queue bound; `close_route`; the two wrap failures; an inline typed
  completion; a deadline; a handle released while its call is held; completions that prepare the next
  call; `onInvalid` (through a test route, since the Runtime refuses a malformed publication); and for
  `routes`, `openRoute` and `closeRoute`, a replayed `request_key`, `close` with a held call and a
  Runtime Control subscription, a Runtime Control subscription ended at its queue bound with the
  refusals inside its end report, and the registration kept after a failed initialization.
  `tests/test_events.nim`'s Capability Authority pass: the typed helper's NOT_AUTHORISED end, also over
  local transport (`test_events_ca_lt`). `tests/test_wipe_routes.nim` W-8: a typed `prepareInvoke` of
  the vault's marked `fetch` leaves no copy of the canary in a released block (orc). `tests/test_hosted_routes.nim` C-14: a consumer written with
  the helpers (`tests/kit/listener_impl.nim`, the beacon kit's provider) hosted and `direct_dynamic`,
  to a direct and a hosted meter, and its failed initialization. Mac: orc, refc and orc-release.
  Confined: `sdk/tests/test_kit_confined.nim` "consumer helpers on the module thread" (a route binding
  the test drives: handlers, ends and completions on the module thread, the full queue, a delivery on
  the module thread queued, the handler rule, a completion inside `submit`, destroy with a live
  subscription and call) and `tests/test_kit_mixed.nim` MX-3 (through the Runtime, `direct_dynamic` and
  hosted: deliveries, a completion, an authority-ended and a full-queue-ended subscription, a route end).
- **Interface-only provider kits** (INTERFACE l.2573, l.2833-2840; §2.6 l.1657-1696). `lcn-gen kit
  --module:NAME [--interface:FILE]… [--supporting:FILE]…` with no PRIMARY generates the kit of a
  binding with no primary document and exactly those implemented interfaces (`acceptBinding`). The
  generators take a `ModuleBinding` wherever they took a set: `documents`, `context` and
  `exposedCount` (`iface/accept`), `callSurface` (`iface/surface`), `validator` (`iface/payload`;
  `ContractValidator.contracts` became `documents`, which nothing read), `nimTypeNames` and
  `nimModule` (`codegen/nimgen`), and `kitMirrors` (`codegen/cmirror`, binding only). The
  interface-only `<module>_types.nim` and kit embed `moduleName`, the interface and supporting
  documents and no primary, and reload them as that binding (`nimrt.loadBindingSchema`,
  `kitrt.loadBindingValidator`); a kit with a primary document emits what it did before, byte for
  byte (every committed fixture regenerates unchanged). The kit's call surface is the interfaces'
  methods and events, its typed functions are the header's `logos_<module-C>_CALL_<interface>_…`,
  and it answers any other method METHOD_NOT_FOUND. A binding with neither a primary document nor an
  interface is no provider (l.2573): its kit exports `_MODULE_name`, `_MODULE_init` and
  `_MODULE_destroy` alone. **`--extends:FILE`** (kit only, repeatable, with or without PRIMARY): an
  earlier contract that the primary or an interface extends, accepted as `acceptBinding` accepts it
  (COMMITMENT §9.1); the descriptor carries it in `extends` (l.1693-1696) and nothing else changes,
  since an entry adds no method or event (l.1695). `--configuration` works for either form.
  Fixtures (`sdk/tests/kit/`, generated into `sdk/tests/generated/`): `metrics_only_module` (the
  §3.9.2 `metrics_provider` alone), `gauge_module` (an events-only interface, `gauge_interface.cddl`,
  extending `gauge_interface_v1.cddl`), `tally_module` (a types-only primary implementing
  `metrics_provider`; its `_implements` literal is the §3.9.2 module's, checked by acceptance), and
  `idle_module` (lifecycle only). Tests: `sdk/tests/test_kit.nim` "interface-only providers and earlier
  contracts" (each descriptor equals the binding's and is accepted with no primary, the right
  interfaces and `extends`; dispatch and the typed function; the sensor's primary method refused;
  typed events-only publication and METHOD_NOT_FOUND for every name; the lifecycle-only table; each
  kit's symbols equal the functions its binding's `lcn-gen types --module` header declares, a confined
  deferred variant adding `_MODULE_async_api`); `sdk/tests/test_kit_dylib.nim` (the interface-only
  kit as a library through its export list, and the lifecycle-only library with no provider symbol);
  `sdk/tests/test_nimgen.nim` (the command line writes the committed files for the four cases and
  refuses `kit` without PRIMARY or `--module`, `nim` without PRIMARY, `--extends` outside `kit`, and
  an earlier contract no described contract extends).
- **Status:** plain consumer helpers built 2026-11-20 (N-1 sub-part 2; I101); the confined mode built
  2026-11-20 (sub-part 3); `invokeAsync` 2026-11-20 (sub-part 4, G338); interface-only provider kits
  and `--extends` 2026-11-20 (sub-part 5).

### G340 — A library leaves its host's signal dispositions alone
- **Kind:** Choice [IMPL] · **Specs:** none; RUNTIME §13 (a host embeds `liblogos_runtime`) and
  INTERFACE §2.6 (a module library is loaded into a host's process).
- **Decision:** every library built here is compiled with `-d:noSignalHandler`: `liblogos_runtime`
  (a compile-time error without it; `nimble build_runtime_lib`, `tests/support/hostbuild.nim`) and the
  kit's module libraries (`tests/support/kitbuild.nim`); `base/libvisibility`, which both import, warns
  when a library is built without it. Otherwise a Nim library's `NimMain` sets handlers for SIGINT,
  SIGSEGV, SIGABRT, SIGFPE, SIGILL and SIGBUS and ignores SIGPIPE for the whole process when it is
  loaded (`system/excpt.nim`, `registerSignalHandler`), replacing the host's. chronos ignores SIGPIPE in
  its own module initializer (`asyncengine.globalInit`); `liblogos_runtime` imports `base/hostsignals`
  before anything that imports chronos, which records SIGPIPE's disposition, and restores it last in its
  initializer. The Runtime's socket writes do not need SIGPIPE ignored (`MSG_NOSIGNAL`, `SO_NOSIGPIPE`,
  `transport/io/sock.c`). A crash inside a library is the host's to report. The programs keep Nim's
  handlers and set their own dispositions: logosd (a signal thread over blocked SIGTERM, SIGINT,
  SIGHUP, SIGUSR1 and SIGUSR2; SIGPIPE ignored; `docs/DAEMON.md` §13), `logos-module-host` (SIGPIPE
  ignored, `host/main.nim`), logosctl, lcn-gen and lcn-pkg (Nim's handlers: a stack trace on a crash).
  A module repository builds its module library with the switch too (the kit's guide, TIER5-PLAN N-1).
- **Test:** `tests/test_host_dylib.nim` "[DECISIONS G340] loading the library leaves the host's SIGINT,
  SIGSEGV and SIGPIPE dispositions as they were": a sentinel handler on each before the load, compared
  after it. It fails without the switch (all three) and without the restore (SIGPIPE). POSIX only.
- **Amended 2026-11-20 (P5, N-1 sub-part 3):** a thread-confined kit imports chronos, whose module
  initializer ignores SIGPIPE, and an author's main module may import chronos before the kit, so the
  import order cannot be relied on there. Kit libraries are built with
  `--import:logos_sdk/base/hostsignals` (`kitbuild`, and the guide's build line), which Nim initializes
  before any other module of the library, and the generated export template calls
  `restoreHostSignals()` last in the library's initializer. `sdk/tests/test_kit_dylib.nim`: a confined
  library whose main module imports chronos first leaves a sentinel SIGPIPE handler in place; it fails
  without the `--import:`.
- **Status:** decided 2026-11-16 by the planning session (N-1 sub-part 1; I101); not a spec matter.

### G341 — The kit's toolchain range, switches, export lists and packaging
- **Kind:** Choice [IMPL] · **Specs:** INTERFACE §2.4, §2.6 (the symbols a module exports);
  TIER5-PLAN N-1.
- **Export lists.** `lcn-gen kit` also writes `<header>_kit.exports` (ld64 `-exported_symbols_list`)
  and `<header>_kit.map` (a GNU version script, `local: *`) from the template's own symbol table
  (`kitgen.kitSymbols`): `_MODULE_name`, `_init`, `_destroy`, `_apply_configuration` when live,
  `_call_surface`, `_free`, `_dispatch` and every typed `_CALL_` function. A library linked with them
  exports its ABI and nothing else: not its `NimMain`, not the C functions it carries that mark
  themselves for export (BLAKE3's here; BoringSSL's or a Rust staticlib's in a port), so two modules in
  one process cannot bind each other's copies. The lists of the meter, sensor, shapes and tuner kits are
  under `tests/generated/` (drift-checked by `test_nimgen`); `buildKitLibrary(…, exports = kit)` links
  with them and `test_kit_dylib` checks through `dlsym` that every listed symbol is found and the
  library's `NimMain` and BLAKE3's functions are not. A Windows DLL exports only what it marks; no list.
- **Toolchain range** (measured on the Mac, N-1 sub-part 1). Kit libraries built by Nim 2.2.4
  (nixpkgs at our pin, without the overlay) beside a 2.2.14 Runtime and Module Host: refc libraries pass
  `test_kit_dylib` and `run.mixed`; orc libraries pass `run.mixed` but crash in `test_kit_dylib`'s
  "calls from threads the library's runtime has not seen", where a context made on one foreign thread is
  destroyed on another after the first has exited. Before Nim 2.2.12 a chunk's owner is the allocating
  thread's thread-local region, which goes with that thread; 2.2.12 pools region handles (reproduced
  alone with a library of two procedures: 2.2.4 crashes, 2.2.14 does not; not a bug to report). And
  Nim#25992 (refc) reproduces on 2.2.4 with its own repro. So the floor is Nim 2.2.14 for refc kit
  libraries (2.2.6 to 2.2.12 not checked) and 2.2.12 for orc ones; `results` 0.5.x. The kit compiles
  under logos-storage-nim's switches (`--styleCheck:usages`, `--styleCheck:error`, `--fieldChecks:on`,
  `ProveField` as an error, `-d:nimTypeNames`, `-d:metrics`, `--tlsEmulation:off`, `-d:release`,
  `--legacy:procParamTypeBackendAliases` from 2.2.12) and logos-delivery's library switches
  (`--deepcopy:on`, `-d:nimOldCaseObjects`, `-d:nimTypeNames`, `-d:metrics`), with `--mm:refc` and
  `-d:noSignalHandler`, under 2.2.4 and 2.2.14. `base/perthread` wraps `GC_fullCollect` in
  `{.cast(raises: []).}`: 2.2.4 does not mark it `raises: []`. `LCN_KIT_NIM=<nim>` builds the test kit
  libraries with another compiler, under `build/kit-dylib/<mm>-nim<version>/`.
- **Packaging:** module repositories take the kit as a nimble dependency (owner, 2026-11-16); its
  package is shaped by the repository split plan.
- **Amended (N-1 sub-part 4, G338):** a kit generated with `--async-api` lists `_MODULE_async_api`
  too. The ledger's lists (`sdk/src/logos_sdk/testing/generated/`) and the confined sensor's
  (`sdk/tests/generated/confined/`) are drift-checked by `test_nimgen`, and `test_kit_dylib` checks
  both libraries' through `dlsym`.
- **Amended (N-1 sub-part 6):** **`kit-toolchains-storage`** and **`kit-toolchains-delivery`**,
  Linux flake checks (one check, `kit-toolchains`, until 2026-11-21, when it was split per set so CI
  builds the two in parallel), build the test kit libraries with the switches the node's libraries build with, on this toolchain (no new compiler
  input): logos-storage-nim `4fe02344`'s (`config.nims`: `--threads:on`, `--tlsEmulation:off`,
  `--opt:speed`, `--excessiveStackTrace:on`, `-d:metrics`, `-d:nimTypeNames`, `--styleCheck:usages`,
  `--styleCheck:error`, `--fieldChecks:on`, `ProveField` as an error,
  `--legacy:procParamTypeBackendAliases`, `-d:withoutPCRE`, `-d:nimOldCaseObjects`,
  `-d:chronosHandleException`, which changes how `async` procs compile, and `-d:release`) and
  logos-delivery `d20ee361`'s library set (`config.nims`, `library/config.nims`: `--threads:on`,
  `--deepcopy:on`, `-d:nimOldCaseObjects`, `-d:nimTypeNames`, `-d:metrics`). Under its set each runs
  `test_kit_dylib` under refc (refc libraries, the confined sensor among them), and `run.mixed` and
  `test_kit_mixed` under orc (refc libraries, the confined ledger among them, in orc Runtimes and
  Module Hosts). `kitbuild` takes the set from `LCN_KIT_SWITCHES`, after its own switches, and builds
  under `<variant>-sw<hash>/`. Linking, `-d:noSignalHandler` and `--import:` of `hostsignals` stay
  `kitbuild`'s, and the memory manager the suite's. Left out as having no bearing on the kit's code:
  the libraries' `-march`, `--debugger:native`, libbacktrace, libp2p's and chronicles' defines.
  **Confined mode's chronos range:** chronos 4.4.x. This repository locks 4.4.1, and confined mode uses
  only API present in 4.4.0 (`ThreadSignalPtr`, `cancelSoon`, `poll`, `getIoHandler`, `close2`,
  `setThreadDispatcher`), so the SDK package can require `>= 4.4.0 & < 4.5.0`. The upper bound's
  reason: inline re-entry polls the dispatcher inside a `poll`, which chronos tolerates only while
  `chronosStrictReentrancy` is off (`config.nim:113`), and a later chronos may turn it on;
  `confinedrt` refuses to compile under it. The libraries' own chronos commits (storage `2d81a762`,
  delivery `0de7b335`, both declaring 4.4.0) are tested by two more checks (G439).
  The guide states the build line and the floor (`sdk/docs/MODULE-KIT.md` §8).
- **Amended (N-1e, G439):** **`kit-toolchains-storage-2d81a762`** and
  **`kit-toolchains-delivery-0de7b335`** run the same suites with the kit libraries built against each
  library's own chronos, and the stew, bearssl or httputils it locks at another revision than core;
  `kit-toolchains-isolated` keeps that to those two checks.
- **Status:** export lists and the Mac toolchain probe built 2026-11-16 (I101, N-1 sub-part 1);
  `kit-toolchains` and the chronos range 2026-11-20 (sub-part 6), the check split per set 2026-11-21,
  the chronos variants 2026-11-21 (N-1e, G439). The packaging is the split's.

### G342 — Modules built with the other memory manager
- **Kind:** Choice [IMPL] · **Specs:** INTERFACE §2.6-§2.8; TIER5-PLAN §7 A7.
- **Decision:** a module library may use either memory manager beside an orc or refc Runtime and Module
  Host: each library runs its own Nim runtime (`--nimMainPrefix`), and only C data crosses the ABI. A
  refc kit module without the confined mode keeps I71's limit (handlers on other threads must not store
  GC'd values). Measured by `test_hosted_routes`' `run.mixed` suite, whose libraries are built with the
  other manager than the suite (`kitbuild.otherMm`): M-1 a hosted meter (sessions, a held call, a
  caller, instance-wide and scoped events, an event published from a thread the module made, channel
  25), a hosted deferred provider, stop and restart; M-2 `direct_dynamic` in process, 8 threads × 50
  reads on their own handles, events delivered on the module's thread, a second instance; M-3 a hosted
  mixed consumer calling a hosted mixed provider.
- **Result:** passes on the Mac under orc (refc modules), refc (orc modules, the inverse pairing),
  orc-release, ASan and TSan, and in the orc and refc variants with modules built by Nim 2.2.4 (G341).
  On x86_64-linux (framework.lan, 2026-11-20, at N-1 sub-part 4's tip 3f739f8) `run.mixed` passes
  under orc, refc and orc-release, as do `test_kit_mixed` under orc and orc-release and
  `test_kit_dylib`'s other-manager ledger in all three; no sanitizer runs there yet. A7's refc host
  flavour is not needed so far.
- **Limits** (accepted by the planning session, 2026-11-16): a refc library is built without the
  sanitizer, beside a sanitized host: refc's conservative stack scan does not see what AddressSanitizer
  moves to its fake stacks, and a refc build under `-d:asan` fails on its own (UBSan: a cell with no
  type in `gc_common.prepareDealloc`, with no other manager in the process). The mixed cases are
  skipped under MemorySanitizer, where the uninstrumented library's writes read as uninitialized (as
  I77's skip list; recorded beside it in `flake.nix`).
- **The confined pairing** (N-1 sub-part 3): `tests/test_kit_mixed.nim`, the ledger fixture (a
  `--confined` kit whose handlers keep GC'd state in the instance) built with the other manager. MX-1
  `direct_dynamic` in this process: two instances at once on their own module threads, 16 threads
  posting at once, events to a subscriber that re-enters from the publisher thread, in a call's scope,
  from a chronos timer, foreign C threads' posts, the host's SIGPIPE kept at load, a stop with
  publications queued, re-creation and 10 start and stop cycles keeping the descriptor count; MX-2 the
  same through a Module Host, and a restart in a new host; MX-3 its consumer side through the Runtime
  (G339). The suite's cases run under an orc Runtime and Module Host only: a refc one refuses every
  route to a contract that marks a payload (G277), as the ledger's `seal` does, so the inverse
  pairing is `sdk/tests/test_kit_dylib.nim`'s, which loads the ledger built with the other manager in
  both builds and posts to it from 8 threads. A refc kit module whose handlers run on other threads
  uses `--confined`.
- **logosd's placements** (N-1 sub-part 6): `tests/test_logosd.nim` configures the ledger, built with
  refc and its export list, as an operator module of orc logosd, `direct_dynamic` (in logosd's own
  process) and `hosted_dynamic` (in a Module Host logosd starts), and calls it through `logosctl call`,
  that is from `lcn_call`'s host: a total kept in its GC'd table across calls, 8 concurrent calls all
  answered on its module thread, an async handler (`wait`, through the deferred surface) and a plain
  one that read `lcn_call` as their caller, a stop and a start again with fresh state, and logosd's
  clean stop with no host left. Under refc both cases skip (G277), and under MemorySanitizer as the
  other mixed cases do.
- **Status:** the reduced form built 2026-11-16 (I101, N-1 sub-part 1); the confined suite 2026-11-20
  (sub-part 3); logosd's placements 2026-11-20 (sub-part 6).

- **Decision:** (c). **Status:** OPEN.

### G437 — What runs while a confined kit's `destroyModule` runs
- **Kind:** IMPL · **Specs:** INTERFACE l.1949-1962 (destroy), l.2116-2117 (work that cannot
  quiesce); RUNTIME l.3713-3716, l.3739; TIER5-PLAN N-1; plan `tier5-plans/stepN-1e-plan.md` §A
  (Fable's P1 on N-3's plan, then Fable's check of the plan).
- **Before.** `destroyTask` set `disposed` before it called the generated dispose, and three paths
  read it: posted callbacks (`post`, `lcn_kit_post`) were dropped, consumer tasks ran with `drop`
  (events, end reports, and the completions of prepared calls and `invokeAsync`), and publication
  replies were never completed. A `destroyModule` that awaited any of them never resumed, and the
  stop deadline ended the host. The guide promised that dropping starts when `destroyModule`
  returns. The order came in with N-1.3 (fdbd7aa), with no reason recorded.
- **Decision.**
  - kitgen's confined template splits the dispose in two. `<prefix>KitDispose` returns
    `destroyModule`'s own future, or nil when `destroyModule` is synchronous; `<prefix>KitRelease`
    does the `GC_unref`. `confinedDestroy(module, dispose, release)` takes both, so every generated
    confined kit is regenerated against it (N-3's and N-4's once their base has this).
  - `destroyTask` awaits that future under `noCancel(join(f))`, so the release is reached even when
    `destroyModule` fails, then sets `disposed` and calls the release in one step, with no await
    between them. The order lives in `confinedrt`, not in each generated kit.
  - While it waits, the context keeps `destroyModule`'s future (`GC_ref`'d). The instance counts as
    released as soon as that future has finished, so what is served in the turns between
    `destroyModule`'s return and the release is dropped as after the release.
  - Two flags. `destroying`, set when `destroyTask` starts: events and end reports (`runEvent`,
    `runEnd`, `runRouteEnd`) are dropped from then on. Released (above): posted callbacks,
    completions (`runDone`, and the kit's own cancellation notice `runCancel`) and publication replies
    run until then. `TaskNode.duringDestroy` marks the two kinds of completion; every other consumer
    task is dropped from the start of destroy. The scoped-publication waits end on the released flag.
  - **A change:** before, events and end reports were still delivered during the unwinding (up to
    2 s, G338), since `disposed` was set after it. Now they are dropped from the start of destroy.
    Nothing a `destroyModule` awaits needs them, and an event handler started during destroy could
    itself be left suspended.
- **What this means for handlers still running.** An `async` handler holds the instance through its
  environment. A plain handler blocked in a nested poll holds only its route's `{.cursor.}`, which orc
  does not count: residual work that existed before, not something every handler is protected from.
  A handler whose unwinding waited for a completion arriving after the 2 s bound now finishes during
  `destroyModule` instead of being abandoned; its invocation still completes once, NOT_READY, since
  `unwindDeferred` leaves what is outstanding to teardown. A handler that ignored its cancellation can
  be woken while `destroyModule` awaits. That is memory-safe for `async` handlers and outside the
  contract (INTERFACE l.2116-2117); timers could already wake it before.
- **For the guide** (MODULE-KIT §3): `destroyModule` may await a callback a foreign thread posts, a
  prepared call's or `invokeAsync`'s completion, and `publishAsync`. Events and end reports are not
  delivered once destroy has begun, and posts still queued when `destroyModule` returns are dropped.
  Whether the Runtime still admits a call made during destroy is another matter: ordinary paths close
  at stop and at shutdown (RUNTIME l.3713-3716), so cleanup that needs another module belongs in a
  preparation method (l.3739).
- **Not covered:** the inner job of an inline re-entry and synchronous entries still running at
  destroy (both still run after `destroyModule`, as G338 records); `isCancelled` for plain handlers
  once destroy has begun; the W-case for marked wipes on the cancellation path (G338).
- **Tests:** `sdk/tests/test_kit_confined.nim` "what runs while destroyModule runs" (8 cases, orc,
  refc and orc-release). The ledger fixture's `destroyModule` is `async` and awaits only when the test
  sets `destroyMode`, so every other case keeps its synchronous behaviour; `foreign_lib.c` gains a
  delayed single post and a stream that posts until stopped. Cases: (a) a callback a foreign C thread
  posts 50 ms in, destroy under 1 s, the instance freed (orc); (b) `invokeAsync` completed by a binding
  thread 100 ms in; (c) `publishAsync`, ok, seen by the publish callback; (d) posts queued by a
  `destroyModule` that returns without yielding never run; (e) events delivered while `destroyModule`
  awaits reach the kit and are dropped; (f) a `wait` 12 handler under `noCancel` whose completion
  comes after the 2 s bound finishes during `destroyModule`, NOT_READY once, the instance freed (orc);
  (g1) a foreign stream `destroyModule` stops and joins, no callback after it returned; (g2) the same
  while `destroyModule` first awaits a delayed post, callbacks during it, none after. Each wait in the
  fixture is bounded by 5 s with `race`, never `withTimeout`, which cancels the call it bounds and
  waits for that. Run by hand once under the order before (`disposed` set at the start of destroy):
  a, b, c, e, f and g2 fail, none hangs; d and g1 pass under both orders.
- **Status:** built 2026-11-21 (Tier 5 step N-1e, part A).

### G438 — Closing a confined kit's module-thread dispatcher, and what destroy left
- **Kind:** IMPL · **Specs:** INTERFACE l.1949-1962, l.2100 (residual work); chronos's main line after
  v4.4.0, which logos-storage-nim (2d81a762) and logos-delivery (0de7b335) pin; TIER5-PLAN N-1; plan
  `tier5-plans/stepN-1e-plan.md` §B (W2-P's P7 check; Fable's checks,
  `tier5-plans/fable-checks/stepN-1e-plan.md`).
- **Found** (W2-P, Mac, 1c0530b). On that line each POSIX dispatcher owns a wake-up descriptor (an
  eventfd on Linux, a socket pair on macOS), and only `closeThreadDispatcher()` closes it. The kit's
  teardown closed the selector and dropped the dispatcher, so every module thread leaked it:
  test_kit_mixed MX-1 counted 41 descriptors against 21 under either library's chronos. On the lock's
  chronos 4.4.1 it passes.
  - **Linux:** confirmed by W2-P's `p7-toolchains` check on framework.lan (2026-11-21,
    `tier5-plans/stepW2-P-spike.md` §2). Without this decision, MX-1 counted 24 descriptors against
    14 under both libraries' chronos: one eventfd per dispatcher.
  - **With W2-P's scratch copy of the fix**, these pass under both: test_kit_mixed (orc) 4/4,
    test_kit_dylib (refc) 16/16, run.mixed (orc) 3/3, and test_kit_confined 39/39 under orc and refc.
    Each kit's C named the library's chronos.
- **Decision.** At teardown, after the kit's own signal is closed (so its registration never counts)
  and the dispatcher's callbacks are cleared, `confinedrt.closeDispatcher`:
  - counts the descriptors left: the open ones (`/proc/self/fd`, `/dev/fd`, else each below
    `min(RLIMIT_NOFILE, 65536)` that `fcntl` accepts) the selector `contains`, less those it held when
    it was made. `moduleMain` now makes the dispatcher before `arm` registers the kit's signal (it was
    made inside `arm`) and notes those: chronos's wake-up descriptor on the main line, none on 4.4.1.
  - On the main line (`when declared(closeThreadDispatcher) and defined(posix)`), when nothing is
    left, checks through chronos's public API only, since its POSIX close raises a Defect on anything
    left and on a failed unregistration (kqueue `getKey`/`addKey`, epoll likewise at 2d81a762): exactly
    one descriptor was noted; the selector `contains` it; `unregister2` of it succeeds; the selector's
    `isEmpty` is read; `registerHandle2` puts it back and `contains` holds again. When all pass and
    the selector was empty, it calls `closeThreadDispatcher()` and writes its diagnostic, if any. Past
    these checks nothing in that close raises.
  - Otherwise, and always on 4.4.1 and on Windows (whose close asserts what cannot be checked first;
    until M12), it takes the old path: the selector's `close2` and `setThreadDispatcher(nil)`. Never
    both.
  - **What is left is never closed.** The kit doesn't own it: the module's stream or a library thread
    may still close it, by when its number may be reused, in logosd perhaps for one of the Runtime's
    own. With no thread left it is a leaked descriptor, not residual work, so INTERFACE l.2100 holds;
    closing it is the module's duty. Unregistering what is left so that the wake-up descriptor could
    still be closed is not done: the scan sees descriptors but not signal or process registrations,
    and chronos offers no full public listing across G341's range.
  - **Reported** in one stderr line, as the kit's fatal path writes, naming the module: "destroy left
    at least N descriptor(s)", a lower bound since a closed descriptor still registered is invisible
    to the scan, or "other registrations" when only `isEmpty` saw something. 4.4.1 exports no
    `isEmpty`, so there a signal, process or closed-but-registered leftover goes unseen.
  - **Strict mode.** Built with `lcnKitStrictDestroy`, the kit aborts after that line, so a module's
    own suite fails at the destroy that missed a close. The define is set only in the test
    configuration files (`sdk/tests/config.nims`, `tests/config.nims`, for in-process kits) and on
    `kitbuild`'s command line, never in the root `config.nims`, which every build reads. `kitbuild`
    builds strict by default (`strictDestroy`); turning it off takes a reason, written beside the
    library (`<name>.lenient`) and to its log, and the variant directory's name says which (`-strict`),
    so a lenient test never loads a strict library of the same name. A strict build holds the marker
    `LCN_KIT_STRICT_DESTROY_BUILD` (`base/testhooks.strictDestroyMarker`); `no-test-hooks` fails when a
    deployment output holds it and requires it in `tests/support/strictprobe.nim` built with the
    define. MODULE-KIT §8: kitbuild never builds a release library. N-4's hosted cases build their
    module with kitbuild, so a registration storage or libp2p leaves at stop aborts them until the leak
    is fixed or the reason recorded.
  - The stderr line carries the module's name: `confinedInit` takes it (`name`), and the generated
    kit passes its `moduleName`, so every confined kit is regenerated.
- **A late cross-thread wake-up** (Fable §6.1). A thread that still holds this dispatcher's handle
  after destroy and calls chronos's cross-thread `callSoon` writes to the wake-up descriptor. Before,
  that descriptor was leaked but open; once closed, its number may be reused, in logosd perhaps for one
  of the Runtime's descriptors. Such a thread is residual work the module must stop or join (l.2100);
  chronos calls closing in that state undefined, and the kit cannot see it, since the cross-thread
  queue is private. This is the risk closing adds. MODULE-KIT §3: before `destroyModule` returns, the
  module stops or joins every thread it gave that handle to.
- **The kit's own posts** never touch the wake-up descriptor: `post`, `lcn_kit_post` and the consumer
  dispatcher's `postTask` check `closed` under the context's lock and only then fire the kit's own
  signal, and teardown sets `closed` before it closes that signal, so a post after the last drain is
  refused and its node freed. A post after `_MODULE_destroy` returned is G440's gate. The window
  between the last drain and the return is too short to hit from a test without a hook in the
  runtime, so G440's foreign-stream case, which posts through the whole destroy, covers both refusals.
- **Amended after the merge** (Fable's review, `tier5-plans/fable-checks/stepN-1e-plan.md` §9; branch
  `stepN-1e-fix`):
  - **The kit's own signal (K1).** chronos's `close` returns before closing when `unregister2` fails,
    and frees the signal either way. Teardown discarded that result, so the kit's own descriptor was
    counted as the module's leftover: the line named the module, and a strict build aborted. Teardown
    now reads the signal's descriptors before the close, through the layout mirror `fire` uses. On an
    error it writes "the kit's own signal could not be closed (<error>); its descriptors stay open and
    out of destroy's count" and leaves those numbers out of the count. It also skips the main line's
    `closeThreadDispatcher`, since one of them may still be registered and that close would raise its
    Defect, and takes the old path instead. It does not abort: the failure is the kit's, not the
    module's.
  - **The dispatcher's identity (K2).** The noted descriptors belong to the dispatcher `moduleMain`
    made, and the kit's signal stays registered with that one. `moduleMain` now keeps it as well
    (`ownDispatcher`, a reference, so a later dispatcher cannot share its address), and teardown
    compares it with the thread's dispatcher. On a mismatch the kit:
    - closes its signal's descriptors directly;
    - writes "destroy found the module thread's dispatcher closed or replaced; the kit counts nothing
      left on it and closes neither dispatcher";
    - drops the thread's dispatcher without closing either one, since it cannot tell what the module
      closed;
    - in a strict build, aborts after the line, as for a leftover.

    chronos itself stops most such modules. `setThreadDispatcher` asserts an empty callback queue,
    which a dispatcher without strict reentrancy never has, because of its sentinel. The main line's
    `closeThreadDispatcher` asserts an empty selector, which the kit's registered signal never leaves.
    Only a module that works around both gets this far. Even then its destroy is reached only if the
    new dispatcher wakes by itself: the kit's signal wakes the old one, so nothing queued is served
    after the swap. If the module dropped its dispatcher altogether, `getThreadDispatcher` makes a
    new one at teardown, and that one is dropped too, with its descriptors still open. MODULE-KIT §3
    now says that a module never closes or replaces its module thread's dispatcher.
    logos-storage-nim's closes are in its `ffi` package (0.3.0, `ffi_context.nim`), registered only
    on the threads that package starts.
  - **A failed init.** On the post-gate, publisher-thread and module-thread failures, `confinedInit`
    closed the signal with chronos's `close`. That close looks the descriptors up in the calling
    thread's dispatcher, and makes a dispatcher if the thread has none. The signal is armed only on
    the module thread, so on these paths it is registered nowhere. `closeUnregistered` now closes its
    descriptors directly and frees it. Windows keeps chronos's close, which never touches the
    dispatcher.

    Checked by reading:
    - logosd's Runtime calls `_MODULE_init` on its lifecycle workers (`runtime/engine.nim`,
      `workerMain`), and the Module Host on its lifecycle thread (`host/main.nim`). Neither file
      imports chronos; core's only dispatcher is the transport's I/O thread.
    - A kit library's chronos is its own copy, so the only dispatcher it ever had on those threads is
      the one that close made.
    - So before this change, the first such failure on each thread left a dispatcher there that was
      never closed. Its epoll or kqueue descriptor stayed open, and on the main line its wake-up
      descriptor too.
  - **`die` on a module thread.** `die` now resets SIGABRT to its default before `abort`, as
    `reportLeft` already did. Without the reset, the host's own handler runs on that thread. A debug
    Nim host's handler allocates, and on a thread its runtime never started it hangs (upstream draft
    190, not filed).
- **For the guide** (MODULE-KIT §3, §8): `destroyModule` closes every stream and transport the module
  opened; a descriptor registered with chronos is unregistered before it is closed; what is left is
  reported and stays open; test builds abort there; threads holding the dispatcher handle are stopped
  or joined first; the module thread's dispatcher is never closed or replaced; kitbuild never builds
  a release library.
- **Tests:** `sdk/tests/test_kit_dylib.nim` "what a confined kit's destroy leaves registered", each
  case in a child process (this program run again) over the strict ledger library and a lenient one
  (`kitledgerp`): `probe` 25 leaves a pipe end registered (the lenient library writes the line, "at
  least 1 descriptor", and returns; the strict one aborts with it); `probe` 26 closes it while still
  registered (on the main line "other registrations", lenient returns, strict aborts; on 4.4.1 no
  line in either mode, as above); a clean destroy writes no line in either mode. `probe` 27 says
  which chronos the library has, since under `kit-toolchains`' variant (G439) the library and the
  host differ. **The 200-cycle case** (moved from N-4; G439 runs it under the variant too): the strict
  confined ledger library initialized, called once and destroyed 200 times in one process (G111),
  after 10 warm-up cycles; the same open descriptors and threads as after the warm-up, and resident
  memory grown by under 1 MiB (it rarely returns to the byte; Mac 2026-11-21: 16 KiB orc, 0 refc,
  16 KiB orc-release). It is the regression check for the wake-up descriptor: without this decision
  each cycle leaks one (Linux) or two (macOS).
  - **The amendment's cases.** Every child now runs under a bound (`leftoverRun`, 120 s by default);
    one that outlives it is killed and fails its case.
    - In `test_kit_dylib`, `probe` 30 has the next destroy replace the dispatcher (destroy mode 10,
      `replaceDispatcher`, with a 2 ms timer that keeps the new one waking). The lenient library
      writes the mismatch line alone and returns; the strict one aborts with it.
    - In `test_kit_dylib`, `probe` 31 posts a null callback on the module thread. The child ends by
      SIGABRT (134) with `die`'s line, within 60 s, in every build mode.
    - In `test_kit_confined`, through the test hooks: `failSignalClose` leaves what chronos leaves
      (the first descriptor open and registered). The destroy writes the K1 line and no "destroy
      left", the strict in-process build goes on, and the descriptor is still open.
    - In `test_kit_confined`, `failInitAt` 1 to 3 on a thread that never had a dispatcher: each init
      fails with its message and no context, and the process has as many open descriptors after it
      as before.
- **Status:** built 2026-11-21 (Tier 5 step N-1e, part B); amended 2026-11-21 (`stepN-1e-fix`: K1,
  K2, the failed init, `die`).

### G439 — A chronos variant in `kit-toolchains`: the kits under the libraries' own chronos
- **Kind:** IMPL · **Specs:** none (a test of G341's range); TIER5-PLAN N-1; plan
  `tier5-plans/stepN-1e-plan.md` §C (W2-P's P7 recipe; Fable, `tier5-plans/fable-checks/stepW2-P-plan.md`
  §8 and `tier5-plans/fable-checks/stepN-1e-plan.md` §8); amends G341.
- **Found** (W2-P, P7). `kit-toolchains` tested switch sets only, always over the lock's chronos 4.4.1.
  logos-storage-nim pins chronos `2d81a762` and logos-delivery `0de7b335`, both on chronos's main line
  after v4.4.0, where each POSIX dispatcher owns a wake-up descriptor (G438). A `--path` in
  `LCN_KIT_SWITCHES` loses to `nimble.paths`, so W2-P's first try compiled 4.4.1 without an error.
- **Decision.** Two more Linux checks beside the per-set ones, one per library revision:
  `kit-toolchains-storage-2d81a762` and `kit-toolchains-delivery-0de7b335`. Each runs its set's suites
  (`test_kit_dylib` under refc, `run.mixed` and `test_kit_mixed` under orc) with the kit libraries built
  against the library's chronos and the packages it locks at another revision than core: storage's stew
  `85c6e313` (0.5.3) and bearssl `38a5622b` (0.2.15); delivery's stew `6a930214` (0.6.3) and httputils
  `97eafdb8` (0.6.0). Core's lock supplies the rest. The host programs keep 4.4.1, as in a node whose
  Runtime is built from core's lock and whose module libraries are built from their own.
  - **The sources** are fixed-output fetches of the commits W2-P fetched under the owner's D-4
    (`tier5-plans/stepW2-P-downloads.md`), each named `<package>-<rev8>` so the kits' generated C names
    the revision. Their hashes match W2-P's checkouts on framework.lan (2026-11-21).
  - **What each library keeps at core's revision:** storage's httputils (0.5.1 `7d771ca3`) and
    delivery's bearssl (0.2.13 `b6c9a389`); results (0.5.1 `df8113dd`) is the same in all three locks.
    Each variant names its kept packages' revisions, and evaluation fails if core's lock moves one: the
    variant would then test a library's chronos beside a package that library does not use, and needs a
    fetch. Storage locks unittest2 0.2.6 where core locks 0.3.0; the variant keeps core's, which no kit
    source imports, so it is in no kit library.
  - **The swap** is the define `lcnKitVariant`, which only kit compiles get (in `LCN_KIT_SWITCHES`). It is
    read by the check's own copy of `config.nims`; the repository's copy is untouched. The copy's paths
    file is `nimble.paths` with each swapped package's entry replaced, never added in front. So no
    module of core's copy can fill a gap in the library's (Fable, `stepW2-P-plan.md` §8).
  - **Asserted in each check:**
    - **The host.** Each suite's host compile (`nim dump` of its own project file, so its directory's
      `config.nims` is in the chain) has the same search paths, lazy paths and defined symbols under the
      check's `config.nims` as under the repository's, and no `lcnKitVariant`.
    - **The kits.** Every kit build is made with `-d:nimBetterRun`, so its nimcache record lists every
      file it read. Every record lists some files; some kit read the variant's chronos; no kit read a
      file of a swapped package from core's set. The property asserted is "removed", not "shadowed".
      These records are used instead of a separate `nim dump`, which would have to repeat kitbuild's
      arguments exactly (Fable, `stepN-1e-plan.md` §8).
    - **The generated C.** The kits' C names the variant's chronos and never core's.
    - Absence is asserted only for the swapped packages; the kept ones are the library's own.

### G440 — A post gate that outlives a confined kit's context
- **Kind:** IMPL · **Specs:** INTERFACE l.2100 (residual work); planning's ruling; TIER5-PLAN N-1; plan
  `tier5-plans/stepN-1e-plan.md` §D (Fable's checks G1-G8, `tier5-plans/fable-checks/stepN-1e-plan.md`
  §7).
- **Found.** A confined kit's poster, `lcn_kit_post`'s `void *` and its consumer dispatcher's
  `context` were the context's own address. A post that came after `_MODULE_destroy` returned (a
  foreign thread the module never stopped, a route handle, subscription or prepared call it never
  released, whose binding still delivers) took a lock in freed memory: in a direct placement,
  logosd's.
- **Decision.** Every such post goes through a gate whose memory is never freed; a late one is
  refused. A refused post is a much smaller failure than a use after free. The same rule Fable gave
  N-3's glue: whatever a late caller checks lives in memory that is never freed.
  - **One pointer-sized value (G1).** The poster, `lcn_kit_post`'s argument and the dispatcher's
    `context` are one value packing a slot of the gate's table (the low 20 bits: about a million
    contexts alive at once) and that slot's generation (the high 44, stored as generation + 1), so it
    is never null: null still means a plain kit, and `post` dies on it. Our targets are 64-bit
    (`static: doAssert`); a 32-bit target would need its own layout. `ModuleServices` keeps the value
    (`gate`), so `poster(s)` and the dispatcher read no context memory, even on a copy of the services
    that outlived destroy; `onItsModuleThread(d)` compares it with the calling module thread's own
    context's.
  - **The table never moves (G2).** A static directory of chunk pointers, 1,024 slots a chunk, chunk 0
    in static storage; another chunk is allocated with the C allocator only when one library has more
    instances alive at once, published with an atomic store and never freed. Zeroed memory is an empty
    table, so nothing needs module initialization. Each kit library has its own table.
  - **A slot** holds a lock, its generation and the live context (nil when none). Free slots are on a
    list under a table lock (an atomic flag), taken only to hand out and take back a slot and never
    held with a slot lock (G3).
  - **Lifetime (G3).** `confinedInit` takes a slot right after the context's locks, before either
    thread starts, since `initModule` may give its poster away at once; no slot is an init failure.
    `freeContext` clears the slot first, under its lock alone, and moves its generation on, so destroy
    (after both threads are joined) and each of `confinedInit`'s failure paths retire it. A slot whose
    generation would pass the maximum is retired, never reused, which closes ABA.
  - **Lock order:** the slot's lock, then the context's, in `post`, `lcn_kit_post` and the consumer
    dispatcher's `postTask`; the slot's lock is held until the context's is released, so the context
    cannot be freed between the check and its use. It cannot deadlock destroy (G4): firing the signal
    does not wait, and destroy takes the slot's lock only after both threads are joined.
  - **Refusals.** A stale generation or a cleared slot is refused. A refused `post` frees its node and
    never calls `fn`; the payload stays the caller's. A refused `postTask` runs its task with drop, as
    a post after the last drain already did, and in both refusals only after releasing the slot's lock
    (G5): the task takes the consumer runtime's locks and may free its owner. That is safe after
    destroy: the owner is kept by its pending count, and the dispatcher record is a value copied into
    each handle, so the context was the only thing that pointed into freed memory.
  - **Every platform.** Only the kit's own locks and C memory, so Windows runs the same code.
  - **The cost:** one more lock per post.
  - **Not a licence (G8).** The gate protects the Runtime's memory. A thread that still posts after
    destroy is residual work (l.2100), and the guide keeps the module's duty to stop posting and
    release its handles before `destroyModule` returns (MODULE-KIT §3).
- **Tests:** `sdk/tests/test_kit_confined.nim` "the post gate", in process, each breaking the module's
  duty on purpose: the packing (never null, a round trip, the largest value fills 64 bits, the last
  generation retires its slot, through `gateNext` with forced generations); `post` and `lcn_kit_post`
  from a foreign C thread after `_MODULE_destroy` returned (refused, `fn` never runs); deliveries, a
  subscription end, a route end and a completion for a handle, subscription and prepared call
  `destroyModule` left unreleased (destroy mode 8; each dropped, the handle's pending count back to 0
  through the consumert test hook `pendingTasks`, no handler runs); the poster an `initModule` gave
  away before it failed (refused); a slot reused by the next context (a generation on; the old poster
  refused, the new one served); and a foreign stream that posts through destroy and on into the
  slot's next context, 20 cycles (destroy mode 9; no callback after the return). The fixture's
  handlers count a call after the return in `lateCalls`. The last case was run once by hand under
  AddressSanitizer and once under ThreadSanitizer before the merge; CI's sanitizer groups run the
  suite.
- **Status:** built 2026-11-21 (Tier 5 step N-1e, part D).

### G318 — The reverse mapper's groups and selection
- **Kind:** IMPL (gaps Q2, Q5) · **Specs:** INTERFACE §3 · **Plan:** `tier5-plans/step5-1-reverse-mapper.md` §4.1. Section and Q numbers below are the plan's; `l.` cites are INTERFACE.
- **Decision.** A group is complete within one header body (Q5; l.2303, l.2313). `--module` and `--subject` select. The reconstruction input is the subject's groups, the supporting groups it references and the groups reached through its contract-header includes; a group merely present is another document, validated only (Q2, l.2325, l.2970). IFC-0801/0802, 0828 and 0830 apply within the reconstruction input. Inference without a role constant needs the whole supplied set to hold one non-common group (l.2337). Comments-document remark 2 (`65d614be`, sharpened in `751b969b`). A header that holds two documents and a dependency include that only one of them references can be reconstructed as a module, or with the referencing document as the subject, and not with the other (l.2282, l.2385); the rejection names the document that references the group
- **Status.** Built in 5-1b (`rmap.nim`); the diagnostic in 5-1c.
- **Amended 2026-11-19 (6cac8335, re-pin P2):** INTERFACE §3.2 l.2244-2246: the subject is mapper input
  and MUST NOT be inferred. The two inference branches (the only module family, the only group) are
  gone; `reconstruct` has no default options, and without `module` or `subject` it refuses with
  `rkSelection` (`lcn-gen cddl` needs `--module` or `--subject`). A selection is an exact name: one that is
  not a valid runtime module name or namespace, or that does not round-trip through its projection,
  matches no supplied document (l.2246). **Reading:** a `--subject` that names a module's primary
  document, declared by the header's `PRIMARY` constant, still reconstructs that module, under the
  module name the header's family gives; the selection is the caller's, and nothing is inferred
  (Fable's review of P2, §9.3). Tests: T4.18b `[IFC-0971] [IFC-0972] [TXT-0055]`, T9.1; every other
  reconstruction in `test_rmap` names its selection from a fixture table.

### G321 — `lcn-gen cddl`
- **Kind:** IMPL · **Specs:** INTERFACE §3 · **Plan:** `tier5-plans/step5-1-reverse-mapper.md` §4.1. Section and Q numbers below are the plan's; `l.` cites are INTERFACE.
- **Decision.** Usage, outputs, the binding summary, `--header`, nothing written on failure, and these limits: 16 MiB and 1,024 headers per input set, include depth 64, parenthesis depth 64 inside a literal, and the §5.3 limits on what is reconstructed. There is no limit on one header: a header is larger than its document, and §3.8 promises the round trip for any conformant schema (IF l.2215, l.2633). The size check before reading uses the running total of the set.
- **Measured (2026-11-18).** One document each, in one process that accepts it, generates its header and reconstructs that header. Every row round-trips with the set limit lifted.

  | Document | Source | Header | Peak memory | Peak over header |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | Map of 32,767 list fields | 644 KiB | 1.67 MiB | 0.25 GB | 142 |
  | 27,823 methods, empty requests and responses (the 1 MiB document limit comes before 65,536 nodes) | 1 MiB | 6.76 MiB | 1.2 GB | 170 |
  | Lists nested 127 deep | 541 B | 0.08 MiB | 9 MB | 104 |
  | 512 maps nested 127 deep, 65,536 nodes, 1-byte names | 267 KiB | 27.9 MiB | 2.0 GB | 68 |
  | Maps nested 127 deep, 1 KiB names | 131 KiB | 23.6 MiB | 1.2 GB | 47 |
  | Maps nested 127 deep, names filling 1 MiB | 1 MiB | 189.9 MiB | 9.6 GB | 48 |

  Two ratios matter. A header dense in declarations peaks at 142 to 170 times its size, and a header dominated by long names at 47 to 48 times. Inline stems repeat the field path, so a header can reach about 190 times its document.
- **The set limit.** 16 MiB, the owner's decision of 2026-11-18. The limit bounds any input, because the mapper parses a set before it can tell that the set is outside §5.3. **The tool can need about 2.9 GB at this limit** (16 MiB at 170 times). 64 MiB could need about 11.4 GB, so a large input could run out of memory instead of failing explicitly (IF l.882). 8 MiB covers the largest flat document, the 27,823 methods, by only 18%; 16 MiB covers it by more than a factor of two. **Still refused, explicitly (`rkLimit`):** a header set over 16 MiB. A set within §5.3 can generate one, for example with inline declarations nested deep (the last three rows; T9.6). The §3.8 round trip is not provided for such a set (`docs/CONFORMANCE.md`).
- **Status.** Built: the input limits in 5-1a, the command in 5-1c (`src/lcn_gen.nim`; tests T9.1 to T9.8).

### G345 — System rules S6–S8
- **Kind:** Choice [IMPL] · **Plan:** `tier5-plans/stepN-2-cli.md` §8. Section and Q numbers below are the plan's.
- **Decision.** §3.8: S6 allows `lcn_call` six Runtime Control methods and no system rule allows another; S7 denies every event outside the events rule and every execution start and stop (`consumer-denied`); S8 bars `logosctl` from reconfiguring or retiring it (`target-denied`); no provider access. An operator rule can allow `lcn_call` further Runtime Control methods, those that need only the Runtime Control decision: `recover_module` is one, since a recovery's execution decision is for the retained origin, not the requester; `lcn_call`'s code calls none of them. R7 (planning's ruling (a), 2026-11-20, with Fable): a method deny cannot be written, since a deny covering a method request covers every event request too and would remove the events rule; logosctl's S3 has the same shape. The clean fix, an event request whose scope a method pattern does not cover (G161; Fable's remark, comments document 29fa2e68), is not N-2's (TIER5-PLAN §8)
- **Status.** Built in N-2b (`compose.nim`); `test_daemon_config` (dc.policy.cli).

DAEMON.md §7a says so.
