Routing** (`runtime/routing.nim`, G254): `lcn.app_config.routing` rules select `local-transport` per (caller, callee); default direct; refused for the Module Loader, Runtime Control as callee, and on Windows. The mode is fixed at establish. **Plumbing** (`runtime/tport.nim`): one transport I/O thread per engine, started at start only when a rule selects local transport; its sink posts `mkIo` to the Runtime inbox, so every I/O event is handled on the Runtime thread (I75); the Runtime thread submits only uncharged commands; a users guard orders `stopTransport` after every port call. `runtime.endpoint_dir` (default `<work_dir>/endpoints`, made 0700 and checked at start) and `lcn.app_transport` (the `TransportConfig` fields; the decoder depth is the engine's, G241). chronos sets SIGPIPE to SIG_IGN for the process when the library loads (documented in HOST-CONFIG). **Transport extensions** (10a code): E1 `cmdPublishConn` (an ordinary Event to one connection's subscriptions); E2 `evPublishResult` for every scoped publication; E3 `logos.schema` goes to the owner as an introspection dispatch and is answered with `cmdIntrospect`; E4 a `HelloCheck` the owner runs after the schema check and before redemption. **Tickets** (`runtime/sessionauth.nim`): a `TicketStore[RouteBinding]` on the Runtime thread, issued at establish and renew of a transported route (min(route end, 60 s) on the engine's monotonic clock); the live answer, with `invocation`, goes to the consumer and the call record; the retained answer is redacted, so a replay has no `invocation` (G255); every route end revokes; `checkDeadlines` sweeps. **Runtime-served endpoint** (`runtime/served.nim`, G257): one per provider realization, made at the first transported establish, stopped when it leaves `ready`, removed with its last session. The engine is its Session Authority: the Hello is judged by `acceptHello` with a state check (route ready and transported to this endpoint, provider realization current, consumer attempt current) before redemption; each Request is an `AsyncCall` with a session origin, admitted by `admit` and run on the call workers, committing under its ticket's lock (a busy budget is retried outside the locks); Cancel commits CANCELLED; a session past its ticket's decision terminates. **Route end** (G260; G174 amended): revocation or expiry answers in-flight Requests NOT_AUTHORISED and terminates; a transport failure closes; a readiness end drains to the stop deadline or shutdown grace. **Ports** (`runtime/ports.nim`): SessionAuthority, EndpointOrders, LinkOrders, `CallRef`, `sessionOrder`, for 4b-3. **Tests**: `test_transported`, `test_host`, `test_transport_io` (E1-E4), `test_transport` (E4), `test_rc_schema` (RUN-0501). **Claims**: RUN-0220, RUN-0226, RUN-0229, RUN-0230 (in §6.2), RUN-0501, RUN-1161, RUN-0543, RUN-0544, RUN-1179, TRN-0153, TRN-0195, TRN-0317, CAP-0254, LDR-0021 (out of inspection); RUN-0045, RUN-0552, IFC-0010 to tier 5; IFC-0524's inspection reason rewritten. **4b-2b. The consumer's transported handle** (`runtime/transported.nim`, engine "Transported route handles"; G164, G256, G258-G260): [IMPL; plan §2.6] the caller half runs on the Runtime thread, which receives every I/O event: one `Link` per materialized handle (one connection, one Hello with the route's one-time ticket, G177's generation), in an engine table by connection id; a materialization and each synchronous call park their reply on the link until its event answers (`rqLinkCall`); asynchronous calls are sent by the Runtime thread, and a prepared one holds its link (`aeLinkHold`, `aeLinkDrop`). The invocation material is kept with the links (G258). The handle has two codes, the route's end cause and the first observed one (G22 re-check); a lost connection is TRANSPORT_ERROR (G256). An asynchronous call cancelled or timed out sends Cancel (IFC-0729). `materialize_route` returns only once the provider holds the session (RUN-0800, RUN-0802). Validation that needs the construction input runs on the consumer's thread (`linkCall`), so a failure carries the same detail as on a direct route. Subscriptions through a transported handle are MODULE_ERROR until 4b-2c. Test hooks under `-d:lcnTestHooks`: `closeSessionsForTests`, `failNextConnectForTests`, `spoilNextTicketForTests`. **Parity suites**: `test_routes_lt`, `test_async_lt`, `test_routes_ca_lt` rerun `test_routes`, `test_async` and `test_routes_ca` with every route to the meter and sensor modules over local transport (unix-stream only); what differs is in `docs/CONFORMANCE.md` ("What 4b-2 changes"): the live answer carries `invocation` and a replay does not (G255); a further handle needs `renew_route` (G258; the fixture renews); the provider's deferred surface serves every Request (the wire does not carry the caller's mode); a call still running past a provider's stop deadline is TRANSPORT_ERROR (G260); events wait for 4b-2c (four cases skipped). **Claims**: RUN-0007, RUN-0008, RUN-0014, RUN-0800 to RUN-0806, TRN-0187, TRN-0191, TRN-0278, IFC-0729 and INTERFACE "Abstract/Execution-Boundary Invariance"; IFC-0480 and IFC-0948 move from inspection to tests. **4b-2c. Events** (engine "Transported events", `runtime/events.nim`, `transported.nim`; G165, G175, G261): [plan §2.7] **provider side**: a session's Subscribe is activated on a call worker (`cjActivate`, `rqActivate`) in a direct subscription's order, with the `subscribe-event` decision (an explicit deny is the SubscriptionResult NOT_AUTHORISED), and recorded on the session before the answer, so a publication that follows the caller's `LOGOS_OK` finds it (Rev R7); Unsubscribe removes it. **Caller side**: `subscribe` through a transported handle checks locally as a direct one does, registers an inactive `LinkSub`, sends Subscribe and returns only after the matching SubscriptionResult, writing the id then (RUN-0192); the Runtime thread activates the subscription before it wakes the subscriber, so an Event that follows is queued. Events are queued per subscription on the Runtime thread and handled by the G178 event workers (`rjLinkDrain`), one drain per subscription, in commitment order; each handled Event releases its credit (RUN-0234). Unsubscribe waits for the SubscriptionResult and for a handler that runs, except its own; the route's end or a release discards queued Events and releases their credits, and no handler starts afterwards (TRN-0290). **Publish adapter** (E1): an ordinary publication reaches direct subscribers first [IMPL], then sends each subscriber connection one Event for its matching subscriptions (RUN-0246), admitted per connection on the Runtime thread (`rqDeliverConn`: both decisions, G175; a subscriber's deny skips that Event only, K40) and submitted with `submitWait(cmdPublishConn, tlClose)` (G165 (a); D3 (a), G261). **Scoped publication over a session** (E2): checked as a direct one, then `cmdPublishScoped` with `tlReport`, and its verdict (`evPublishResult`) awaited: OK; NOT_READY after the Response or CANCELLED was committed or the connection closed; NOT_AUTHORISED after an authority end or a denied `publish-event`; MODULE_ERROR when too large. A new connection never inherits a destination (RUN-0832). **Shutdown** (plan §2.9): handles observe NOT_READY before any realization is destroyed; sessions drain within the grace; link subscriptions end with their links; a publication still waiting for a verdict is answered NOT_READY when the Runtime thread leaves. **The ends of a route, one row each** (`ports.EndPolicies`, `engine.routeEnd`; the table is in G260; G174 (a); owner batch B 7; RUNTIME l.621, l.623, l.1065, l.3224, l.3226-3227, l.3850; TRANSPORT l.543; INTERFACE l.2101): revocation and expiry terminate; a transport failure, a serve failure, K12 and an establishment that issued no ticket close at once, as will, in 4b-3, a side whose process or host is gone; the others drain, each to its own bound: `close_route` (`stop_deadline` from the end [IMPL]), a provider stop (the provider's stop deadline), shutdown (the grace), a consumer stop (the consumer's stop deadline), and a consumer or provider failure (the drain deadline of the failed instance's cleanup release, here `stop_deadline` from the end [IMPL]). Batch B 7 named only the provider stop, shutdown and `close_route`. The consumer's stop and failure and the provider's failure are our choice within G174 (a) (Fable, 2026-11-13): **listed for the owner's next approval**. At every end, admission closes at once, each in-flight invocation is marked cancelled and its provider notified, and nothing waits past the bound. **Tests**: `test_transported` (the 4b-2c cases, among them a consumer stop, a consumer failure and a provider failure that drain; the `bulk` kit module publishes an Event of any size), `test_events_lt`, `test_events_ca_lt`, and the event cases of `test_async_lt` turned on. Parity differences (CONFORMANCE): handlers run on event workers after the publication returned (two direct-only cases skipped in `test_events_lt` and `test_events_ca_lt`, two in `test_async_lt`); a subscriber's explicit deny at delivery keeps the subscription (K40). **Claims**: RUN-0192, RUN-0234, RUN-0246, RUN-0832, TRN-0290; G165 and G261 built | 2026-11-13 |

Direct mode.** `app-config.v1` `permissions` selects the profile (`EngineConfig.permissions`, `AuthorityWiring.profile`) and provisions new instances, by instance, else by module (G110); `create` refuses repeated entries, an entry naming the Module Loader or another module's instance, settings that are unordered, undefined, non-conforming or not enforced, and an orchestration or authority instance without the minimum. `runtime/settings.nim`: the state (revision, permissions, `pending`/`applied`/`failed`), a replacement's status and its settlement (G281, G285), and the `prm` side record (`store.cddl` `lcn.prm_record`), written for every instance before it is first committed and before each reply, deleted at retirement; at open the settings are restored, a `pending` one settled, and a store the selection cannot read refused. Module.** `lcn_orchestrator`, a consumer-only kit module (`src/logos_core/orchestration/`, façade `orchestration.nim`), linked in and registered by a host as the `direct_static` binding `lcn_orchestrator` (`orchestratorStaticSymbols()`); the host's `orchestration` field gives it the role, its name confers nothing (G53, l.189-192). It calls only through its Runtime Control binding (l.184), with `kit/rcclient.nim` (typed synchronous calls, prepared asynchronous calls, subscriptions; responses copied to shared memory on the completing worker); nothing in it imports the engine, the host or the plumbing. **Configuration.** `lcn_orchestrator.config` (`orchestration/config.cddl`, generated through `nimble regen` like every kit): `authority`, `defaults` (start or stop), `ordering`, `restart` (`disabled` or `backoff`), per-instance `overrides`, `resync_ms`. No exclusion: its own instance and the Module Loader are always left out (G191, G246). Package default backoff 1 s × 2 up to 60 s, 8 attempts, stable after 60 s; resync 30 s; bounds checked by `settingsOf` (an invalid value fails `_MODULE_init` with MODULE_ERROR); startup-only. `orchestratorDeclaration()` gives a host the declaration, with the package default as `default_value`. **Accounting.** `orchestrator-state.cbor` in its state directory (`orchestration/state.cddl`, format `logos-core-nim.orchestrator-state.v1`): one open episode per instance and intent revision (attempts, calls, the last call's wall time, `pending`), written before each charged `recover_module`; a refusal refunds the attempt, an answer that never arrived is charged once and read again (C-9); another Runtime's file is discarded; a broken file or a failed write fails closed (no call is made); revisions are never counted (TL-08, G227). The directory is locked (`<dir>/lock`) while the instance lives; with no state directory it refuses to start unless every policy is `disabled`. **Behaviour.** One worker thread per instance (released per thread at its end). `get_self` first; the authority's bring-up when one is named (`start_module`, then polls, 100 ms doubling to 5 s); the binding inferred from the first `list_modules {limit: 1}` that succeeds (G290); then subscriptions to the module-state, execution-state, inventory and configuration-state events, a full traversal (`list_modules` pages of 256) and the first pass. Events are hints: handlers copy bytes into a 64-slot ring and the worker reads (`get_readiness`) before it decides; a full ring forces a resync. A periodic resync (`resync_ms`) subscribes anew before it unsubscribes the old ids and traverses everything (G225). Decisions (`orchestration/policy.nim`, pure) from lifecycle state, intent and the `cleanup-timeout` classification only (G291, RUN-1055): startup defaults are requests guarded by the revision read with `uninitialized` (K15, a Reading: l.194, l.2247, l.2261, l.1913); `stopped` closes the episode; a live `error` is recovered on the backoff, charged, up to `max_attempts`, then a diagnostic; `ready` for `stable_ms` closes the episode; a dependent waits until every prerequisite is `ready` (G287); probes and resumption per G288 and G289. The engine is unchanged. **Deviations from the plan.** The schemas use `uint32` and `uint64` where the plan wrote `uint` (lcn-gen maps no bare `uint`); the lock file is `<dir>/lock` (`durable.acquire`); `encodeSettings` and `orchestratorDeclaration` return a `Result`; an asynchronous call that cannot be prepared is a refusal (attempt refunded, retried after `initial_delay_ms`); past 4096 open episodes no new one is opened (a diagnostic, retried at the resync); after a dropped answer the restarted module's first read is its traversal. Gate: RUN 771/771 (67 deferred to Tier 4b); merged with 4b-2a, RUN 780/780 (56). **4b-5c. Permission resumption** (2026-11-14, after 4b-4; RUNTIME l.2590-2604, l.3754-3756, l.3801-3804; G284, G288, G291 as amended). The module subscribes to `permission_settings_changed_event` (P5's events, now five) and takes it as a hint, like the configuration event: a change of an instance's settings brings its next probe forward to `max(last call + initial, now)`, never sooner. With 4b-4's admission, an instance a settings replacement stopped is `unloaded`, intent and origin kept (RUN-0914, RUN-1066); while its settings lack host-ambient each probe is refused NOT_AUTHORISED (`authority-denied`, G284), uncharged and never exhausted; once they settle `applied` with it, the event brings the recovery forward. A startup default the settings refuse leaves intent `requested` (G284), so it is resumed the same way. **G291 amended (owner, 2026-11-14, "Do a, as Fable recommends"):** rule 4g reads a closed set of four `error` classifications as a resumption (`ResumableFailures`, `resumable` in `policy.nim`): `cleanup-timeout`, `permission-enforcement-failed`, `authority-denied`, `authority-evaluation-failed`, so an overrun followed by a refused or denied probe stays a resumption, under `disabled` too. Every other classification, an unrecognized one included, is a live failure (l.3756). A resumption accepted that then fails is an execution failure under the restart policy (l.3804): charged under `backoff`, not retried under `disabled`. Found while building: a test that withdraws a permission right after the engine shows `ready` can race the module's own read, so the start still counts toward the probe spacing; the case waits for that read. CI on 5ddd886 (2026-11-15, x86_64 orc-release) found another race of that kind: a probe is counted when the module sends it, and four cases read the count, then replaced the settings while the last probe could still be in flight. Decided after the replacement, that probe is the resumption itself: the instance came back with no further probe, and `recovers == before + 1` failed (3 against 4; reproduced on a Mac by sending each recovery 300 ms after it is counted). In the same run the refused startup default came back only at its next scheduled probe, 12.85 s after the replacement, as if the settings hint had had no effect; that did not reproduce (with an answer or a hint 300 ms late the hint stays in force), so its cause is open. The four cases now wait until every counted probe is answered (`settled`, from the module's diagnostics) before they act, and the two resumption cases print the module's and the engine's diagnostics if a check fails. CI on b3af640 (2026-11-16, x86_64 orc) showed that cause: the module's own resync. A resync subscribed anew and then ended the old subscriptions. Ending a subscription discards what its queue holds (RUNTIME l.3426 asks only for resubscription and a fresh query), and the traversal after it decides from readings alone. So a settings event the Runtime had queued but not yet delivered was lost, and the probe it would have brought forward waited for its schedule (12.82 s; no subscription-loss diagnostic). It reproduced on a Mac with every event drain starting 150 ms late (resync 200 ms): both resumption cases failed in every run, at 12.8 s. Now [IMPL] a resync ends the generation before the current one and keeps the current one for one more interval. Meanwhile both generations deliver each event, and a hint is idempotent. A rescan that a hint asks for (an inventory event, a full ring) reads everything again without subscribing anew. An event is now lost only if its delivery takes longer than one resync interval. With the same delay, both cases pass; with only the rescan change, they still failed. A new case keeps a settings event queued across a resync by starting each drain half an interval late (`setRcDrainDelayForTests`, a Runtime test hook in `rcevents.nim`). **Tests:** `test_orchestration` suite "resumption when permissions become available" (ten cases: a settings event still queued when the module subscribes anew; a permission withdrawn and given back; a refused startup default resumed; a refused probe is not a failed resumption, an accepted one that fails is charged; under `disabled` it is not retried; `disabled` end to end after an overrun, for failed settings and for a denial; the hint's floor under a burst of settings events; an explicit stop ends the probes; the engine routines that set the three authority and permission kinds, pinned); `test_orch_policy` (the closed set). **Documents.** HOST-CONFIG ("What it decides from", "Events are hints", "Probes", "When permissions become available", the five events), CONFORMANCE, SPEC-STATUS, README, G288, G291, inspection R-q. **Claims.** RUN-0696. CONFORMANCE "Claims", `conformance/claims/RUN.toml`'s header, HOST-CONFIG "Orchestration duties" and DEPLOYMENT.md §0 say so; the facts block's `runtime_claim` is compared with logosd's composition by test_deployment's [TXT-0350] test. | 2026-11-14 |

| I104 | IMPL | The re-pin to logos-lips `6cac8335`: the pending list (plan `tier5-plans/repin-6cac8335.md` §2, sub-step plan `tier5-plans/repin/P0.md`) | **P0** moves the pin, syncs the ledgers and restamps the generated files; no parser, mirror file, pin value or behaviour changes. What still follows the previous text is listed in `spec/repin-pending.toml`, and `spectrace mirror`, `pins`, `gate` and `deploydoc` accept only what is listed. `spec/repin-baseline.toml` is the frozen copy, with its SHA-256 in `tools/spectrace/spectrace.py`: `spectrace pending` requires each baseline entry to be open on its own sub-step or to have left with the evidence its kind needs. A change of sub-step needs a `[[moved]]` record. A unit leaves as claimed with a test that can run or an inspection item with a reason, or by name in its claims file with a decision row that names it. A stale id leaves with a record of what replaced the rule. A text entry of class `behaviour` clears only by a test tagged `[TXT-nnnn]`, unless a decision row that names it lowers the entry. A `todo` entry may clear by a typed reading (`reword`, `removed`, `informative`, `holds`) that says what was compared, and a guarded entry also names the test or code site that was read. Merged sub-steps go in `closed`, and plain `spectrace pending`, which CI runs, fails while one owns an entry. **Known limit:** no static check can tell a real test from an empty one, so `spectrace pending --step` prints all the evidence a sub-step used for its review. **Note at re-pin P9 (2026-11-20, 6cac8335).** Every sub-step has merged, so `spec/repin-pending.toml` holds `[deferred]` only: the 53 units and 19 text entries that stay deferred past the re-pin. `spectrace pending` refuses any other section, `closed` included. **What went:** the `[mirror]`, `[pin]`, `[units.*]`, `[stale]`, `[deploydoc]` and `[[text]]` sections, and their handling in `spectrace mirror`, `pins`, `gate` (the held status, the stale exemptions and the list's own checks) and `deploydoc`, which are back to their forms before P0; sub-steps, `closed` and their order; `[[moved]]` and the rule that an entry keeps its sub-step; `--step` and its evidence report (each sub-step's output was kept with the P9 report, after the spot-check of the readings). **What stays:** the frozen list and its digest; `[deferred]`'s rules (each owner one of the work items; each unit a live gated requirement that its claims file defers by name; a unit or text entry that joined it has a decision row that names it; a text entry rides on a unit of its spec and section, or of a spec and section its sentence names, deferred to the same work item); "neither deferred nor cleared" for every frozen text entry; the reading checks (what was compared, the kind, the guard's site, the reword's pair, the removed side, a `holds` reading's named test); each cleared entry's suite still names its tag; and a text entry leaves `[deferred]` only when a test of its unit carries its tag. **The leaving rules.** A unit the re-pin tracked (the frozen list's `[units]` and `[deferred]`, and each `[[units]]` record) whose claims file still defers it must be in `[deferred]`; "still defers" is any `deferred:` status, and as the gate closes tiers 1 to 4b only `deferred:tier-5` is left. A unit leaves claimed, with a test that can run or an inspection item with a reason, and a changed unit keeps its record of what was compared. The rules are not symmetric: the six units of the frozen list's `[deferred]` leave only claimed, while the 47 that joined later from `[units]` or by a `[[units]]` record may also leave with another status named in their claims file and a decision row that names them (as when a dropped work item's units go out of scope), which `[units]` allowed when they joined. **A text entry's cleared record, once it leaves `[deferred]`,** is `id`, `step` (the work item that claimed its unit, such as `5-3a`) and `test` (the suite in which one test carries both tags); the tool checks `test`, not `step`. **`deploydoc`** now matches a duty row's citation whole in BCP-0038's reasons, so a short citation is not met by a longer stale number or a range (`names_cite`). The checks on `spec/repin-text-cleared.toml` keep its 221 tags in test names, and its 248 readings checked, until the next revision's pending file replaces them. | 2026-11-18 |

Until then both paths, the direct Runtime (`runtime/events.nim`) and the Module Host (`host/rcbinding.nim`), return INVALID_PARAMS for a null user data, an event name that fails INTERFACE §1.5 and a null or empty payload, and `LOGOS_OK` otherwise, whatever the fan-out did: only the two codes of l.3351. Whether `s` is a copy is the compiler's cursor inference (the probe, under the free scan, orc and orc `-d:release` alike): a `var` local is copied; a `let` local is not, except inside a loop; a field of a `var` object, a `var` parameter and a plain parameter are not; `discard ?f()` drops a copy. An object, tuple or array constructor passed to a non-sink parameter borrows its fields and is not destroyed (Nim 2.2.14 `compiler/injectdestructors.nim` l.884-929). Not a Nim bug: the copy is results' own `TODO avoid copy`, and zeroing before release is G276's requirement, not the language's. **Nine paths fixed**, each with a case that fails without its fix: (1) `abi/checks.providerChecked` zeroes a status outside the provider set in place, not in a copy; (2) `codegen/consumert.completeTyped` zeroes the checked completion status and erases a failure's text once `onDone` returns; (3) `iface/outcome.checkDetail` zeroes the decoded detail tree; (4) `codegen/kitrt` registers `releaseLastFailure` with `onThreadRelease`, so the per-thread failure text is cleared at a thread's end (`a71ebac`); (5) `runtime/invoke.commitSync` zeroes a provider's failure when the route's end decides a synchronous call; (6) `transport/envelope.failureOf` zeroes a refused failure; (7) `transport/hello.readFirst` zeroes the first frame's tree, and the payload and failure text of a first message that is not a Hello (`wipeRefused`); (8) `transport/session.onResponse` zeroes the failure text of a Response for no outstanding request; (9) `host/consumer.setFailure` zeroes the `clip` copy. Tests: `test_wipe_routes` gains the matrix steps `outside` and `detail` (W-4, W-6, W-7, and W-7's hosted consumer through the probe's new `call-quiet`), a W-4 `commitSync` case and a W-8 typed-failure case; `test_wipe` W-2 gains three refused-message cases. **Four found safe** by the rule: `transport/session.nim` :540 `encoded(Message(... response: resp))` and `checkStatus`'s `checkFailure(InvocationFailure(...))` (constructors passed to non-sink parameters), `checkFailure`'s `let m = f.message.get` (a cursor), and `readDetail`'s `view` (a template over `toOpenArray`); the md lists the sites that never see marked text. **Out of scope**, with reasons: ticket copies on the Hello path (R18: a ticket exists only transiently; fix 7 zeroes a received Hello's tree); the carrier's frame copies (no marked payload crosses the carrier, I92); `host/rcbinding`'s `clip` temporaries (Runtime Control marks nothing). **Handed on:** `cli/` is a consumer like any other, so G276 applies to `lcn_call`.
